issue.page_hint: Ch 17, §17.8 mini-case, 'Initial sizing analysis' and 'Decision' (page not determinable from chunk)
issue.quoted_clause: the integer-slot FP8 bound under **no-reuse** is **99 working hosts at the 70% × 95% policy, plus one spare host for N−1 operation: 100 hosts in total**
issue.observed: The mini-case's Decision sizes the agentic fleet from the KV-residency screen alone. The chapter's own §17.4 rule — 'The fleet is governed by the *minimum* of several independent ceilings, not by KV alone', with (b) 'prefill compute capacity' as a named screen — is never applied to the agentic trace, even though the agentic trace's prefill demand is 4.6x the single-shot demand (41,990 vs 9,200 tokens/request).
issue.evidence: Recomputed from the chapter's own inputs. Agentic T=3 no-reuse prefill per request = 41,990 tokens (§4 ledger). At 100 rps: 100 x 41,990 = 4.199M prefill tok/s. Host prefill ceiling (case (i), 35% MFU) = 19,780 tok/s (§17.4(b)). Hosts at full utilization = 4,199,000 / 19,780 = 212.3; at the u x rho = 0.665 policy = 212.3 / 0.665 = 319.2 -> 320 working hosts. The KV screen gives 99. So the prefill screen is ~3.2x the KV screen and binds. At 40 rps: 40 x 41,990 = 1.6796M / 19,780 = 84.9 -> /0.665 = 127.7 -> 128 hosts vs the KV screen's 82. Under the 100%-reuse policy: 100 x 11,600 = 1.16M / 19,780 = 58.6 -> /0.665 = 88.2 -> 89 hosts vs the KV screen's 79 — still binding. The FP8 KV lever (the mini-case's headline lever) does nothing for the prefill screen, so the mini-case's conclusion that 'KV precision and prefix caching are the primary levers that make agentic fleets affordable' is not supported for the no-reuse case.
issue.root_cause: The mini-case reuses the non-agentic §17.4 screen set (KV only) rather than the chapter's stated min-of-ceilings rule; the prefill screen was computed only for the 9,200-token single-shot request.
issue.correction: Add the prefill-compute screen to the agentic sizing in §17.8 (and to Table 17-2's scope note), for both reuse policies and at 40/100/200 rps, under cases (i)/(ii)/(iii). Restate the Decision as max(KV screen, prefill screen, decode screen) and re-derive the headline host count. If the prefill screen binds, say so and revise the 'KV precision and prefix caching are the primary levers' conclusion for the agentic case.
issue.acceptance_test: A reader can recompute, from numbers printed in §17.8, a prefill-screen host count for the T=3 no-reuse trace at 100 rps and see that it exceeds the KV screen; the Decision paragraph prints max(KV, prefill) rather than the KV screen alone.

issue.page_hint: Ch 17, §17.8 mini-case, 'Initial sizing analysis' and 'Decision'; F-01 box
issue.quoted_clause: At T = 3 (the 95th-percentile, and the honest stress-cohort sizing point — "worst case" applies only to the 2% fallback route, F-01) ... This is a KV-residency planning minimum, not a validated deployment size.
issue.observed: The Decision provisions a fleet sized from the T=3 stress cohort substituted into a Little's Law mean equality — exactly what the chapter's own F-01 box says is invalid ('Little's Law needs the **mean** E[W_KV-resident]; a percentile substituted into a mean equality yields a stress bound, not a measured/typical population'). F-01 computes the distribution-weighted mean W (~12.71 s) but never converts it into a fleet size, so the chapter's correction never reaches its own recommendation. The Decision also labels a conservative upper bound a 'planning minimum'.
issue.evidence: Using F-01's own ledger: mean W = 0.68x11.52 + 0.25x14.56 + 0.05x17.70 + 0.02x17.40 = 12.71 s. At 100 rps, in-flight = 1,271. Mean per-request KV (incl.-output convention, from the §8 ledger's classes 10,365 / 11,230 / 12,095 / 11,795 tokens) = 0.68x27.16 + 0.25x29.42 + 0.05x31.69 + 0.02x30.90 = 28.03 GB -> C = floor(436/28.03) = 15 (FP16), floor(436/14.01) = 31 (FP8). FP8: N = ceil(1,271 / (31 x 0.665)) = ceil(61.65) = 62 working hosts. FP16: N = ceil(1,271 / (15 x 0.665)) = ceil(127.4) = 128 working hosts. The stress-cohort figures are 99 (FP8) and 205 (FP16). So the mean-based fleet is ~62 vs the stated 99 (FP8) and ~128 vs 205 (FP16) — a 37- and 77-host difference. (Using the ledger's mixed KV convention instead gives a mean of 27.3 GB -> C = 15/31 -> 71 FP8 hosts; the range 62-71 is the honest one.)
issue.root_cause: The stress cohort was carried from the sizing table into the Decision without the mean-based alternative that F-01 mandates; the two ledgers are kept separate in F-01 but only one is used for the purchase decision.
issue.correction: Print both ledgers' host counts in §17.8 (mean-based and T=3 stress cohort), state which one is being provisioned and why (e.g. 'we provision the stress cohort because the fallback tail is unbounded'), and replace 'KV-residency planning minimum' with a label that matches the quantity (a conservative upper bound on the required fleet under the stress cohort).
issue.acceptance_test: The Decision paragraph contains a mean-based host count derived from F-01's 12.71 s ledger, and the words 'minimum'/'upper bound' match the quantity being quoted.

issue.quoted_clause: the token volume that fleet serves at the canonical workload — 6.24M requests/month × 9,500 tokens ≈ 5.93×10¹⁰ tokens/month — giving ~$155,817 ÷ 5.93×10¹⁰ ≈ **$2.63/1M** ... at the canonical volume (6.24M requests/month × 9,500 tokens ≈ 5.93×10¹⁰ tokens) the same per-token delta scales to ≈ $69,654/month
issue.observed: The 'canonical volume' used for the fleet-amortized per-token rate and for the canonical-volume savings is 6.24M requests/month, which is inconsistent with the canonical workload's own stated '~10 rps average' unless a duty cycle is stated — and none is. Two derived, decision-relevant numbers ($2.63/1M and $69,654/month) scale linearly with this basis, and the chapter's 'closeness is a coincidence of this volume' argument depends on it.
issue.evidence: Canonical average 10 rps over 30 days = 10 x 2,592,000 s = 25.92M requests/month; over 730 h = 26.28M. The printed 6.24M requests/month implies 2.37 rps average (6.24M / 2,592,000 s), i.e. 4.15x below the canonical average, and a peak-to-average ratio of 40 / 2.37 = 16.9x. At 25.92M requests/month the fleet-amortized rate would be $155,817 / (25.92M x 9,500 / 1e6) = $155,817 / 246,240 = $0.63/1M (not $2.63/1M), and the mixed-fleet saving would be 246,240 x ($2.50 - $1.325) = $289,332/month (not $69,654/month). The 32-host variant would likewise be ~$0.96/1M, not $4.01/1M. The chapter's own arithmetic is internally consistent on the 6.24M basis; the question is whether that basis is the canonical one.
issue.root_cause: The monthly volume basis was carried into Ch 18 from Ch 16 without reconciling it against the canonical '10 rps average' stated in Ch 4/Table 4-2 and repeated in Ch 17, Ch 18 and Ch 19.
issue.correction: State the canonical monthly volume and its duty cycle explicitly (e.g. '10 rps is the peak-window average; the monthly volume is 6.24M requests over X active hours'), or correct the volume. Then recompute the $2.63/1M fleet-amortized rate, the $4.01/1M 32-host variant, and the $69,654/month saving on the stated basis, and re-check the 'coincidence' argument against the $2.50/1M table row.
issue.acceptance_test: One monthly volume figure appears in Ch 4, Ch 16, Ch 17 and Ch 18, and the $2.63/1M, $4.01/1M and $69,654/month figures reproduce from it.

issue.page_hint: Ch 17, §17.4, 'Effect on the headline counts' (decode-leg bullet) vs Table 17-1
issue.quoted_clause: A decode step must re-read every resident sequence's KV: bytes/step = 140 GB + B × 24.9 GB, so at the canonical B = 17 a step reads ≈ 563 GB and takes ≈ 563 GB ÷ 26.8 TB/s ≈ 21 ms/step
issue.observed: The service time W is derived from a decode step evaluated at B = 17 (the KV-slot ceiling), while the provisioning policy operates the host at C x u x rho = 11.3 concurrent sequences. At 11.3 sequences the same model gives a materially faster step and a shorter W. The chapter never states which operating point W is evaluated at, and the two give different fleet sizes.
issue.evidence: At B = 11.3: bytes/step = 140 + 11.3 x 24.9 = 421.4 GB; step = 421.4 / 26.8 TB/s = 15.7 ms; W = 1.08 + 300 x 0.0157 = 5.8 s; in-flight at 40 rps = 232; N = ceil(232 / 11.305) = 21 working + 1 = 22 total — versus the headline 31 working / 32 total. At B = 17 the chapter's own numbers give W = 8.6 s and 32 total. The chapter's sensitivity band also holds B fixed at 17 while varying the step time, so the band and the policy are on different operating points.
issue.root_cause: The u x rho slot derate and the W model were derived independently and never reconciled; the chapter does not say whether u is a sustained-utilization target (host fills to C at peak) or a hard cap on resident sequences.
issue.correction: State explicitly whether W is evaluated at the KV-slot ceiling (B = C = 17, conservative for fleet size) or at the policy operating point (B = C x u x rho = 11.3), and print the alternative fleet count so the reader can see the size of the effect. If the intent is 'sustained target, peak fills to C', say so and note that the decode step at peak is the 21 ms figure.
issue.acceptance_test: §17.4 names the concurrency at which W is evaluated, and the sensitivity band and the headline use the same stated operating point.

issue.quoted_clause: under **100% prefix reuse** only the final call's new context is prefilled — 11,600 tokens, i.e. 2,400 new tokens (3 × 800 of retrieved context) once the 9,200-token prefix is served from cache
issue.observed: The sentence is self-contradictory and mis-describes the policy that produces W = 14.14 s. If the 9,200-token prefix were 'served from cache', the prefill would be 2,400 tokens, not 11,600. The 14.14 s figure corresponds to prefilling 11,600 tokens (the 9,200 base once, plus 3 x 800 of new retrieved context), which is Ch 19's stated convention.
issue.evidence: Ch 19 §4: 'Under a 100% prefix-reuse policy only the incremental prefix (9,200 + 3×800 = 11,600 ...) is pre-filled, giving W_reuse(3) ≈ 14.14 s'. Recomputed: 11,600/9,200 x 1.08 = 1.3617 + 0.025 x 495 (12.375) + 3 x 0.133 (0.399) = 14.136 s = 14.14 s. If the prefix really came from cache (2,400 tokens prefilled): 2,400/9,200 x 1.08 = 0.2817 + 12.375 + 0.399 = 13.06 s. The two readings differ by 1.08 s, which changes the reuse-column host counts (e.g. FP8 at 100 rps: ceil(1,306/17.955) = 73 vs the printed 79).
issue.root_cause: The phrase 'served from cache' was used for 'prefilled once and reused across calls', conflating a per-request cache hit with intra-request prefix reuse.
issue.correction: Rewrite as: 'under 100% prefix reuse the 9,200-token base is prefilled once and reused by every subsequent call; each later call prefills only its new 800-token delta, so total prefilled = 9,200 + 3 x 800 = 11,600 tokens'. Keep the same wording in Ch 19 §4 and Ch 19 Table 19-1's note.
issue.acceptance_test: The reuse policy is described identically in Ch 17 §17.8, Ch 19 §4 and Table 19-1, and 11,600 tokens is the only prefilled total any of them quotes.

issue.quoted_clause: plus the ledger's ~200 ms guardrail evaluation + re-dispatch term ≈ **17.60 s** end-to-end
issue.observed: The fallback's end-to-end service time adds only the ~200 ms guardrail/re-dispatch term to the model-side W, omitting the 660 ms of agent-orchestration overhead that the same mini-case's ledger records for the fallback class. The chapter's own convention (W excludes L_agent; end-to-end = W + added orchestration) is not applied.
issue.evidence: The §8 ledger's fallback row gives 'Added orchestration: 660 ms + ~200 ms ≈ 860 ms'. W_fallback = (39,395/9,200) x 1.08 + 0.025 x 495 + 3 x 0.133 = 4.6247 + 12.375 + 0.399 = 17.399 s (~17.40 s, as printed). End-to-end = 17.40 + 0.86 = 18.26 s, not 17.60 s. The printed 17.60 s equals 17.40 + 0.20 only.
issue.root_cause: The 'end-to-end' figure was assembled from the W term plus one of the two orchestration components, without cross-checking against the ledger row that defines the fallback's added orchestration.
issue.correction: Print the fallback's end-to-end service time as W + 860 ms (~18.26 s), or state explicitly that the quoted 17.60 s excludes the 660 ms orchestration and is therefore not an end-to-end figure. Apply the same check to the completed T=3 class.
issue.acceptance_test: For every class in the §8 ledger, the quoted end-to-end time equals the class's W plus that class's ledger added-orchestration value.

issue.page_hint: Ch 19, §4 'Multi-step reasoning cost' (scope note after the W(T) equation)
issue.quoted_clause: the quadratic attention term adds +17.2% at 9.2K under case (ii) and grows with context, giving $W_\text{no-reuse}(3) \approx 18.68$ s under case (ii) and $\approx 18.19$ s under case (iii) rather than 17.70 s
issue.observed: Neither printed value is reproducible from the stated factors. 'Grows with context' is not a law, and the two numbers imply a specific (unstated) growth model that differs from the quadratic behaviour the sentence names.
issue.evidence: Uniform application of the case (ii) factor 1.1723 to the prefill sum gives 4.9293 x 1.1723 = 5.7786 s -> W = 5.7786 + 12.375 + 0.399 = 18.55 s, not 18.68 s. The printed 18.68 s is reproduced only if the attention surcharge grows LINEARLY in context, i.e. factor_k = 1 + 0.172 x (I_k / 9,200): sum = 10,782.4 + 11,959.2 + 13,163.0 + 14,395.8 = 50,300 -> /9,200 x 1.08 = 5.9048 -> W = 18.679 s. The printed 18.19 s is reproduced by the same linear law with the case (iii) surcharge 0.0861: 4.9293 x (1 + 0.0861 x 1.15071) = 5.4178 -> W = 18.192 s. A genuinely quadratic surcharge (factor_k = 1 + 0.172 x (I_k/9,200)^2) gives 18.84 s, not 18.68 s.
issue.root_cause: The case (ii)/(iii) FLOP-counting conventions were applied to a per-call context-length series without stating how the surcharge scales with context, and the resulting numbers were not re-derived from the printed factors.
issue.correction: State the growth law explicitly (e.g. 'the attention surcharge is modelled as growing linearly with context: factor_k = 1 + p x I_k / 9,200') and print the per-call factors so 18.68 s and 18.19 s reproduce. If a quadratic law is intended, recompute and print the resulting values.
issue.acceptance_test: A reader can reproduce 18.68 s and 18.19 s from the printed factors and the stated growth law, term by term.

issue.page_hint: Ch 17, §17.4, 'The fleet is governed by the *minimum* of several independent ceilings'
issue.quoted_clause: (c) **decode bandwidth/compute capacity** → ÷ 300 tokens per response (the HBM-bound decode roofline), and (d) the **observed p95-TTFT/TPOT SLO goodput** under a load test
issue.observed: The chapter names four ceilings and then closes the screen set with only two of them. The decode screen (c) is never converted into a host count, so the reader cannot verify that the decode leg does not bind — even though the chapter devotes a detailed bullet to the decode bandwidth model and shows that the peak decode demand (12,000 output tok/s) cannot land on one host.
issue.evidence: From the chapter's own decode model: at B = 17 and 21 ms/step, a host emits 17 / 0.021 = 809.5 output tok/s. Peak demand = 40 rps x 300 = 12,000 tok/s. Hosts at full utilization = 12,000 / 809.5 = 14.8 -> 15; at the u x rho = 0.665 policy = 14.8 / 0.665 = 22.3 -> 23 working hosts. At the 25 ms budget pole (680 tok/s/host) the policy figure is 17.6 / 0.665 = 26.5 -> 27. Both are below the KV screen's 31 working hosts, so the decode screen does not bind — but that conclusion is currently the reader's to guess.
issue.root_cause: The min-of-ceilings list was written as a taxonomy rather than as a closure, and the decode bullet was placed in a different subsection (the TPOT-budget bullet) without being folded back into the screen set.
issue.correction: Add the decode screen's host count (no-derate and policy) to the screen table and state explicitly that it does not bind at the canonical peak, with the numbers. Do the same for the agentic case, where the decode screen's B and step time differ.
issue.acceptance_test: All four named ceilings appear with a host count, and the chapter states which binds and which do not, with numbers.

issue.page_hint: Ch 18, §3.1, bullet list under 'With 8×H100 (640 GB), we can simultaneously run the weights of:'
issue.quoted_clause: **290 GB < the canonical 436 GB KV budget, so the FP16 tier cannot co-reside at the canonical profile.**
issue.observed: The sentence is ambiguous in a way that inverts its meaning. The FP16 tier's weights ARE in the co-resident list immediately above (140 GB), so 'cannot co-reside' is false as written; what is true is that the shared pool's KV falls from 436 GB to 226 GB (C from 17 to 9), so the FP16 tier cannot be served at the canonical 9,500-token concurrency. The next sentence states the correct version, so the paragraph contradicts itself.
issue.evidence: The co-resident list totals 140 + 70 + 70 + 70 = 350 GB; 640 - 350 - 64 = 226 GB KV; C = floor(226/24.89) = 9 vs the canonical 17. The chapter's own next sentence says 'the pool's KV falls to ~226 GB and C to ~9'.
issue.root_cause: A compressed summary sentence was written before the precise statement and left in place.
issue.correction: Rewrite as: 'the FP16 tier's weights are resident, but the shared pool's KV falls from 436 GB to 226 GB (C from 17 to 9), so the FP16 tier cannot be served at the canonical 9,500-token concurrency in this placement.'
issue.acceptance_test: The paragraph contains one statement of what cannot co-reside, and it agrees with the co-resident list and with the C = 9 figure used downstream.

issue.quoted_clause: the 18–27 extra hosts' amortization plus energy (≈$134–200K/mo at the Ch 16 per-host basis) exceeds the ≈$69.7K/mo saving, so the total-cost sign is undetermined until a marginal per-host cost is supplied (break-even ≈ $69,654/18 ≈ $3,870/host/mo)
issue.observed: The paragraph computes the extra-host cost on the Ch 16 per-host basis, shows it exceeds the saving, and then concludes the sign is undetermined pending a marginal per-host cost. Having just used the per-host basis, the sign is determined on that basis: negative (the mixed fleet costs more). The conclusion contradicts the arithmetic immediately preceding it, and the break-even figure ($3,870/host/mo vs the Ch 16 basis of ~$7,420/host/mo) already settles it.
issue.evidence: Ch 16 per-host basis implied by the chapter's own numbers: $155,817 / 21 hosts = $7,420/host/mo. 18 extra hosts x $7,420 = $133,560 (~=$134K); 27 x $7,420 = $200,340 (~=$200K). Break-even = $69,654 / 18 = $3,870/host/mo, which is 52% of the $7,420 basis. So on the stated basis the mixed fleet's total cost exceeds the single-model fleet's by ~$64K–130K/month.
issue.root_cause: The paragraph hedges a conclusion it had already computed, in order to avoid committing to a placement recommendation; the hedge contradicts the numbers it prints.
issue.correction: State the sign on the Ch 16 basis (the shared placement is more expensive by $64K–130K/month at the canonical volume), then state what would change it (a lower marginal host cost, a higher token saving, or the dedicated placement's 29-vs-31 working-host result). If the intent is that the per-host cost is not yet known, remove the $134–200K figures.
issue.acceptance_test: The paragraph's conclusion follows from the numbers printed in the same paragraph, and the break-even figure is compared against the same per-host basis used for the extra-host cost.

issue.page_hint: Ch 17, §17.4, 'Recomputed at the canonical peak under this policy' paragraph
issue.quoted_clause: **policy $u \times \rho$ working = 31, + $N_\text{spare}$ = 32 (KV-only, case (i))** ... **Two coincidences to keep straight: the u-only KV screen and the case-(i) prefill screen both give 29, and the KV-only policy total and the case-(iii) prefill screen both give 32 — same numbers, different screens.**
issue.observed: The label '(KV-only, case (i))' attaches the prefill FLOP-counting case label to the KV screen, which the same chapter says is case-independent ('the KV screen alone — case-independent (case (i) labels only the prefill screen)'). The reader is given two contradictory statements about what 'case (i)' means within one section.
issue.evidence: The chapter defines case (i)/(ii)/(iii) as the prefill FLOP-counting convention (linear-only / full-square / causal-triangle) in §17.4's feasibility check and in Table 17-2's caption. The KV screen involves no FLOP count, so it has no case.
issue.root_cause: A parenthetical was added to disambiguate a coincidence and accidentally reused the case labels.
issue.correction: Replace '(KV-only, case (i))' with '(KV-only, case-independent)' and keep 'case (i)' exclusively for the prefill FLOP-counting convention throughout Ch 17.
issue.acceptance_test: Every occurrence of 'case (i)/(ii)/(iii)' in Ch 17 refers to the prefill FLOP-counting convention, and the KV screen is never labelled with a case.

issue.page_hint: Ch 18, §3.2 'Per-token cost (example numbers, Q4 2026 pricing)' table
issue.quoted_clause: | Model | Token cost (USD / 1M) | Per-request service latency (ms) | Basis |
issue.observed: The latency column header does not carry the scope that the chapter's own bases box and §3.4 note supply (TTFT for a short-prompt routing scenario, not full generation, not the canonical 8.6 s service time). The table is the artefact readers copy into a routing table; read on its own, 120/250/300/800 ms reads as full request latency, which §3.4 shows is off by ~146x for the CPU tier.
issue.evidence: §3.4: 'under a full-generation reading the CPU tier's 4-bit model (~35 GB ÷ ~75 GB/s ≈ 0.47 s/token) would need ~117 s for 250 tokens, ~146× the printed 800 ms, so only the TTFT reading is defensible.' The bases box repeats the scope, but neither is attached to the table.
issue.root_cause: The scope note was placed in prose around the table rather than in the table's own headers.
issue.correction: Rename the column to 'Per-request service latency (ms) — TTFT, short-prompt routing scenario' and add a footnote to the table repeating the scope and the 146x full-generation caveat. Consider adding a 'Basis' entry for the FP16 row's rate and latency, which currently lacks the [ILLUSTRATIVE] label the other rows carry.
issue.acceptance_test: The table's headers alone are sufficient to prevent a reader from treating the latency column as full-generation latency.

issue.quoted_clause: The minimum bandwidth is B_min = φ · λ · D (the fleet aggregate derived in §17.4.4 — ...) ... the per-request transfer leg must also fit (§17.4.4).
issue.observed: Both references point to §17.4.4, but the interconnect-budget material is the third of the five subsections of §17.4 (Per-host throughput and KV cache budget; Load-balancer overhead factor; Cross-host interconnect budget; Request traffic and model collectives; Counter-scenarios). If the subsections are numbered 17.4.1–17.4.5, the correct reference is §17.4.3.
issue.evidence: Subsection order in the chunk places 'Cross-host interconnect budget' third under §17.4; §17.4.4 would be 'Request traffic and model collectives are different populations', which contains no D, B_min or t_net arithmetic.
issue.root_cause: Subsection renumbering during restructuring left the cross-references stale.
issue.correction: Renumber both references to the interconnect-budget subsection, and check every §17.4.x reference in Ch 17, Ch 18 and Ch 19 against the final subsection numbering.
issue.acceptance_test: Every §17.4.x reference resolves to a subsection that contains the cited material.

issue.quoted_clause: far beyond one host's ~436 GB KV budget, so **agents do not just stress memory, they force a fleet** (Chapter 17)
issue.observed: The claim is contradicted by Ch 17, which establishes that the non-agentic canonical workload already forces a 21-host (31 working / 32 total) fleet at the canonical peak. The agentic layer raises the requirement; it does not introduce it. As written, the sentence tells the reader that the fleet requirement is a consequence of adding agents, which is the opposite of Ch 17's headline finding ('A single host is not viable at peak even for the non-agentic canonical workload').
issue.evidence: Ch 17 §17.3: 'A single host is not viable at peak even for the non-agentic canonical workload — the fleet needs roughly ⌈344/17⌉ = 21 hosts at 40 rps'. Ch 19's own numbers: 86 in-flight x 24.9 GB = 2.1 TB single-shot at 10 rps average, already ~5 hosts; agentic T=1 raises it to ~115 x 27.2 GB = 3.1 TB, ~8 hosts.
issue.root_cause: A chapter-local rhetorical contrast was written without checking the preceding chapter's conclusion.
issue.correction: Rewrite to: 'the fleet requirement is already set by the non-agentic workload (Ch 17); the agentic layer multiplies it — at the canonical peak the agentic T=3 profile raises the KV-resident population several-fold, so agentic depth is a fleet-sizing multiplier, not a fleet trigger.'
issue.acceptance_test: Ch 19's fleet claim is consistent with Ch 17's finding that the non-agentic workload already requires a fleet.

issue.quoted_clause: Latency: 85 ms (local PostgreSQL on H100 host) [ILLUSTRATIVE][ASSUMPTION] ... λ_tool ≈ 100 ms (typical, tool backend range 50–150 ms) ... W's tool leg is Chapter 17's ~133 ms/turn tool/retrieval-only rate ... Chapter 17 §8 itself notes that a single model should use one rate consistently
issue.observed: Three different tool rates are in simultaneous use (85 ms in the §3 trace, 100 ms in §4's L_agent, 133 ms/turn in Ch 17 §8's W), and the chapter states the rule that forbids this ('a single model should use one rate consistently') and then does not follow it. W(3) = 17.70 s — the number that drives the entire agentic fleet sizing in Ch 17 — depends on the 133 ms rate, while the chapter's own tool-latency model says 100 ms.
issue.evidence: W(3) = 4.9293 + 12.375 + 3 x 0.133 = 17.703 s. With the chapter's own λ_tool = 100 ms: 4.9293 + 12.375 + 0.300 = 17.604 s (~17.60 s), which changes the Ch 17 agentic host counts: at 100 rps, in-flight 1,760 instead of 1,770 -> FP8 N = ceil(1,760/17.955) = 99 (unchanged after the ceil), but at 40 rps in-flight 704 -> ceil(704/8.645) = 82 (unchanged); the reuse column moves: 100 x 14.04 = 1,404 -> ceil(1,404/17.955) = 79 (unchanged). The counts survive, but the printed W and the printed rate disagree, and the reader cannot tell which rate is canonical.
issue.root_cause: The tool leg was defined in Ch 17 (tool + retrieval + re-ranking = 133 ms) and in Ch 19 (tool backend round-trip = 100 ms) without a mapping between them, and the reconciliation paragraph diagnoses the problem instead of resolving it.
issue.correction: Publish one mapping: e.g. 'λ_tool = 100 ms is the tool-backend round-trip; the W tool leg of 133 ms is the mean of tool round-trip plus retrieval/re-ranking (33 ms)'. Then state which rate enters W and which enters L_agent, and confirm that the two are not double-counted. Apply the same rate to the §3 trace's 85 ms (or explain why a local PostgreSQL query is faster than the mean).
issue.acceptance_test: One tool-rate table exists in Ch 19, every printed tool latency maps to a row in it, and W's tool leg is computed from a named row.

issue.quoted_clause: Under case (i) the prefill leg leaves ~7% headroom and does not bind against the 21-host KV screen — only cases (ii)/(iii) bind, and there the policy screens already reported in Table 17-1 carry the extra hosts (29 under case (i), 32 under case (iii), 34 under case (ii)).
issue.observed: The parenthetical lists the case-(i) policy screen (29) among the screens that 'carry the extra hosts', immediately after stating that case (i) does not bind. 29 is below the KV policy screen of 31, so it carries no extra hosts. The reader is given a list of three numbers in which one is explicitly excluded by the sentence that introduces it.
issue.evidence: Policy screens: KV = ceil(344/11.305) = 31 working; case (i) = ceil(18.606/0.665) + 1 = 28 + 1 = 29; case (iii) = ceil(20.21/0.665) + 1 = 31 + 1 = 32; case (ii) = ceil(21.81/0.665) + 1 = 33 + 1 = 34. Case (i) is below the KV screen; case (iii) ties it (31 working); case (ii) exceeds it (33 working).
issue.root_cause: The parenthetical was assembled as a complete list of policy screens rather than as a list of binding screens.
issue.correction: Restate as: 'case (i) does not bind (28 working vs the KV screen's 31); case (iii) ties it (31 working); case (ii) binds (33 working, 34 with the spare).'
issue.acceptance_test: Every screen listed in the sentence is one the sentence says binds.

issue.page_hint: Ch 18, §3.1, '8-bit KV headroom (the row's own fit test)' paragraph
issue.quoted_clause: the tier needs ≥2 GPUs (160 GB, 3 concurrent) or must be declared short-prompt-only. Minimum placement is ⌈(70 + 24.89)/80⌉ = 2 GPUs.
issue.observed: The parenthetical is ambiguous: '160 GB, 3 concurrent' reads as 160 GB of KV (which would give 6 concurrent), whereas 3 concurrent comes from 160 - 70 = 90 GB of KV headroom. The two sentences also apply different criteria — the parenthetical is a concurrency fit, the formula is a one-request fit — without saying so.
issue.evidence: 160 GB total - 70 GB weights = 90 GB KV; 90 / 24.89 = 3.62 -> 3 concurrent. 160 / 24.89 = 6.43 -> 6 concurrent if 160 GB were KV. The formula ceil((70 + 24.89)/80) = ceil(1.186) = 2 is a 'one canonical request must fit' criterion, which happens to give the same answer.
issue.root_cause: A compressed parenthetical mixes total GPU memory with KV headroom.
issue.correction: Rewrite as: 'the tier needs >= 2 GPUs (160 GB total -> 90 GB KV headroom -> 3 concurrent canonical requests); the minimum placement that admits even one canonical request is ceil((70 + 24.89)/80) = 2 GPUs.'
issue.acceptance_test: The parenthetical distinguishes total GPU memory from KV headroom, and the two placement criteria are separately labelled.

issue.page_hint: Ch 17, §17.4, 'Effect on the headline counts' (TPOT-budget bullet)
issue.quoted_clause: the canonical SLO pole is 40 ms/token (Ch 15 §1), and it is in the band below.
issue.observed: 'it is in the band below' is ambiguous: it can be read as 'the 40 ms pole appears in the sensitivity band listed below' (correct) or as 'the 40 ms pole lies below [something]' (incorrect). In a sentence whose whole purpose is to fix the sizing pole, the ambiguity is costly.
issue.evidence: n/a — wording.
issue.root_cause: Compressed cross-reference to the immediately following list.
issue.correction: Rewrite as: 'the canonical SLO pole is 40 ms/token (Ch 15 §1), which appears as the top of the sensitivity band below.'
issue.acceptance_test: The sentence has one reading.

issue.quoted_clause: Alerts should trigger when per-host concurrency exceeds 80% of C, when LB error rate exceeds 0.1%, or when cross-host bandwidth utilization exceeds 70%.
issue.observed: The concurrency alert threshold (80% of C = 13.6 slots) sits above the chapter's own operating point (C x u x rho = 11.3 slots), so the alert would fire only after the host has already exceeded its policy operating point. The other two thresholds are relative to their own budgets; this one is not.
issue.evidence: C = 17; 0.8 x 17 = 13.6; policy operating point = 17 x 0.70 x 0.95 = 11.305. At the T=3 stress point the operating point is 13 x 0.665 = 8.645, so 80% of C = 10.4 is again above it.
issue.root_cause: The alert was written against the raw slot count rather than the effective slot count the chapter defines.
issue.correction: Express the threshold against the effective operating point (e.g. 'per-host concurrency exceeds 90% of C x u x rho') or state that 80% of C is a hard-ceiling alarm distinct from the policy alarm.
issue.acceptance_test: Every alert threshold in §6 is expressed against a quantity the chapter defines elsewhere.

issue.quoted_clause: This flips the original conclusion: the fleet is not a distant luxury but a necessity at the canonical peak, driven by the product of service time (8.6 s) and arrival rate.
issue.observed: 'the original conclusion' has no referent in the chapter or in the surrounding text the reader has seen. It reads as an artefact of an earlier draft, and it invites the reader to hunt for a conclusion they have not been given.
issue.evidence: n/a — wording.
issue.root_cause: Revision residue.
issue.correction: Replace with a self-contained statement: 'This reverses the intuition that a single 8xH100 host can serve the canonical peak: the fleet is a necessity at the canonical peak, driven by the product of service time (8.6 s) and arrival rate.'
issue.acceptance_test: No sentence in Ch 17 refers to an 'original' or 'previous' conclusion without naming it.

issue.page_hint: Ch 17, Table 17-2, row 'in-flight @ agentic no-reuse W=17.70s'
issue.quoted_clause: | in-flight @ agentic no-reuse W=17.70s | 708 | 1,770 | 3,541 |
issue.observed: The 200-rps cell is not reproducible from the printed W: 200 x 17.70 = 3,540, not 3,541. The value is reproducible only from the unrounded evaluator output (17.7033 s -> 3,540.7 -> 3,541). The chapter's closing note says 'in-flight counts are rounded to the nearest integer (708 / 1,770 / 3,541)', which invites the reader to reproduce it from the printed W and fail.

issue.correction: State in the table note that in-flight counts use the unrounded evaluator W (17.7033 s), or print 3,540. The same applies to the reuse row (200 x 14.14 = 2,828, which does reproduce).

issue.quoted_clause: | 70B dense FP16 | $2.50 | 120 | capital + energy |
issue.observed: The FP16 row's rate and latency carry no evidence label while the three rows below it carry '[ILLUSTRATIVE] example rate, Q4 2026 — not retrieved'. The FP16 row is the row the whole chapter's comparison is anchored on (it is the single-model baseline and the reference for the $2.63/1M 'coincidence'), so it is the row most in need of the label.
issue.evidence: n/a — labelling consistency.
issue.root_cause: The label was added to the derived rows but not to the baseline row.
issue.correction: Apply the same label to the FP16 row, or state once in the table caption that all rates and latencies are illustrative worked-example inputs (which the §3 bases box already says) and remove the per-row labels for consistency.
issue.acceptance_test: All four rows of the §3.2 table carry the same evidence-label treatment.

issue.page_hint: Ch 19, §8 mini-case, note under the unconditional fallback-inclusive ledger table
issue.quoted_clause: (The T = 1 and fallback rows quote the last retained context without a separate terminal answer on top — the fallback never makes a synthesis call — which is why they sit ~0.8 GB below Table 19-1's 27.2 GB at the incl.-output convention.)
issue.observed: The note explains the convention offset for the T=1 and fallback rows but not for the T=2 row, which has the same offset (28.6 GB in the ledger vs 29.4 GB in Table 19-1). A reader comparing the two tables row by row finds one unexplained 0.8 GB discrepancy.
issue.evidence: T=2: ledger 10,930 x 2.62 MB = 28.64 GB; Table 19-1: 11,230 x 2.62 MB = 29.42 GB; difference 0.78 GB, the same as T=1 (27.16 vs 26.37).
issue.root_cause: The note was written to explain the two rows that looked anomalous and the third was overlooked.
issue.correction: Generalise the note: 'the T=1, T=2 and fallback rows quote the last retained context without a separate terminal answer, so they sit ~0.8 GB below the corresponding Table 19-1 values.'
issue.acceptance_test: Every row of the §8 ledger reconciles with the corresponding Table 19-1 row under one stated convention.

issue.quoted_clause: In our example, consolidation wins on token rate because the 8-bit and MoE tiers together capture ~90% of request classes at lower cost than FP16; the FP16 tier still handles the tail without contention.
issue.observed: 'without contention' is asserted for the shared placement the chapter adopts, but in that placement all tiers share 226 GB of KV (C = 9) and the FP16 tier's 10% share (34.4 in-flight) competes for the same slots as the other tiers. The chapter's later paragraph concedes this ('that group, not a 2-GPU reserve, is what "handles the tail without contention" above'), leaving the earlier claim standing on an unsupported footing.
issue.evidence: Shared pool: C = floor(226/24.89) = 9 slots for all tiers; FP16 tail demand = 4 rps x 8.6 s = 34.4 in-flight = 3.8 hosts' worth of the shared pool.
issue.root_cause: The sentence was written for the dedicated placement and carried into the shared-placement discussion.
issue.correction: Qualify the claim to the dedicated placement, or state the shared-placement contention explicitly (the FP16 tail consumes ~3.8 of the pool's 9 slots per host).
issue.acceptance_test: Every placement-dependent claim in §3.5 names the placement it holds under.

issue.page_hint: Ch 18, §3.1 'Hardware capacity mapping' table, 4-bit GGUF row
issue.quoted_clause: ~18 by weights alone; ~5 if the 436 GB canonical KV budget is reserved for the active tiers; the worked deployment reserves 2
issue.observed: The '~5' figure is derived from reserving the canonical 436 GB KV budget, but the co-resident deployment actually adopted in the same section leaves 640 - 280 (FP16 + 8-bit + MoE 8-bit) - 64 = 296 GB for 4-bit weights, i.e. ~8 copies. The three figures in the cell are computed against three different placements and none is labelled.
issue.evidence: 640/35 = 18 (weights alone); (640 - 436)/35 = 5.8 -> 5 (canonical KV reserved); (640 - 280 - 64)/35 = 8.4 -> 8 (the actual co-resident list).
issue.root_cause: Three placement scenarios were folded into one cell without labels.
issue.correction: Label each figure with its placement ('weights alone', 'canonical KV reserved', 'co-resident list as adopted') and state which one the deployment uses.
issue.acceptance_test: Each number in the cell names the placement it assumes.

issue.page_hint: Ch 17, §17.4, 'At the canonical peak' bullet list
issue.quoted_clause: With C ≈ 17.5 per host (FP16 KV) at full utilization, the minimum N = ⌈344/17⌉ = **21 hosts**
issue.observed: The sentence quotes C as 17.5 and then divides by 17 in the same breath, with the rounding rule explained elsewhere (§17.3). A reader who divides 344 by 17.5 gets 19.7 -> 20 and cannot reconcile the printed 21 without finding the floor rule in another subsection.
issue.evidence: 344/17.5 = 19.66 -> 20; 344/17 = 20.24 -> 21. The chapter's rule is 'floor the slot count before the ceil'.
issue.root_cause: The continuous quotient and the floored slot count are both carried in the same sentence.
issue.correction: Write 'with C floored to 17 whole-context slots (17.5 continuous), the minimum N = ceil(344/17) = 21'.
issue.acceptance_test: Every host-count sentence names the floored slot count it divides by.

issue.page_hint: Ch 17, §17.4, subsection heading 'Per-host throughput and KV cache budget'
issue.quoted_clause: ### Per-host throughput and KV cache budget
issue.observed: The heading promises per-host throughput; the subsection derives only the KV-slot ceiling C and the per-request KV. The per-host throughput (C/W ~ 2.0 req/s) is derived in the reconciliation box and in the 'Small queueing counterexample' subsection instead. The heading is the reader's index for what the subsection delivers.
issue.evidence: n/a — structure.
issue.root_cause: The subsection absorbed the reconciliation box without its heading being updated.
issue.correction: Rename to 'Per-host KV cache budget and the implied request rate', or move the C/W derivation into this subsection so the heading matches the content.

issue.quoted_clause: Acceptable for interactive chat (typical threshold: ≤500 ms).
issue.observed: The 500 ms interactive threshold is used as a decision gate in §3.3 (the 4-bit tier is excluded because it 'would miss the 500 ms interactive threshold'), in §3.5 (the consolidation latency criterion) and in §8 (the mini-case's SLO), but it is introduced as a 'typical threshold' with no source and no label, unlike the other illustrative inputs in the chapter.
issue.evidence: n/a — evidence labelling.
issue.root_cause: A scenario SLO was introduced without the chapter's standard [ILLUSTRATIVE][ASSUMPTION] treatment.
issue.correction: Label the threshold [ILLUSTRATIVE][ASSUMPTION] and state that it is the deployment's own SLO to be set from the user experience, not a universal constant — consistent with the treatment of the 200 ms and 2 s figures in §18.2.
issue.acceptance_test: Every threshold used as a decision gate in Ch 18 carries an evidence label.

issue.quoted_clause: With the illustrative φ = 0.05 — halved from §17.6's φ = 0.1 to model a lower cross-host fraction at the grown 100-rps traffic
issue.observed: The φ = 0.1 value originates in §17.4's interconnect-budget subsection; §17.6 restates it in the architecture-consequence section. The reference resolves to a section that contains the number, so it is not broken, but it points the reader at the wrong origin for a parameter they are about to change.
issue.evidence: n/a — cross-reference.
issue.root_cause: The mini-case was written after §17.6 and referenced the nearest occurrence.
