issue.issue: The figure's internal annotations ('many query heads -> few shared KV heads', 'query heads', 'shared KV heads', and the boxed '8 query heads : 1 KV head (x 8 groups)') are set noticeably smaller than the figure title and smaller than the caption text, and appear to fall below the 8 pt print floor for figure in-text annotations. issue.evidence: Relative type sizes on the rendered page: figure title is clearly the largest; the subtitle and the three coloured labels plus the boxed note are roughly 60-70% of the caption's size. The house convention sets an 8 pt floor for figure in-text annotations.
issue.acceptance_test: Measure the rendered font size of every string inside the figure (subtitle, 'query heads', 'shared KV heads', boxed note) and confirm each is >= 8 pt at print size; enlarge if not. Note that this check is an estimate from a downscaled render and must be repeated on the print-resolution PDF.

issue.figure: FIGURE 7.6 — 'Memory floor: inference vs fine-tuning (canonical 70B, FP16 unless noted)'
issue.issue: The five-line note block below the chart and the red annotation 'full fine-tune exceeds an 8xH100 box: needs multi-node or offload' are set in small type, below the caption's size, and the note block carries the figure's most important scoping statements (what is and is not included). At print size these are the hardest text on the page to read.

issue.issue: The caption states the per-request KV price is "24.9 GB/request max-fp16 KV (0.5K max context, per Fig 7.6)". 0.5K = 500 tokens; at the book's canonical 2.62 MB/token FP16 KV that is 1.31 GB/request, not 24.9 GB. The figure's own arithmetic (436 / 24.9 = 17.5) and FIG 7.8 on the facing page (the identical 24.9 GB block labelled "9.5K context") both require 9.5K tokens: 24.9 GB / 2.62 MB per token = 9,504 tokens. As printed, the caption's stated context length is wrong by a factor of 19 and a reader who recomputes from it gets C ~ 333 instead of 17.
issue.evidence: Caption on PDF p.154 / printed p.134. FIG 7.8 on PDF p.155 / printed p.135 labels the same 24.9 GB KV block "9.5K context" and derives 32K -> 84 GB and 128K -> 335 GB from the same 2.62 MB/token, which is mutually consistent only at 9.5K. 24.9 GB / 2.62 MB = 9,504 tokens.
issue.acceptance_test: Caption reads "9.5K max context" (or "9,504 tokens"); a reader recomputing 9.5K x 2.62 MB = 24.9 GB reproduces the figure's 17.5 -> 17 exactly; the string "0.5K" no longer appears anywhere in the Ch 7 KV-price derivation.

issue.issue: In the figure's arithmetic line the operator between "436 GB" and "24.9 GB" is not legible as division at the supplied render size; it reads as "+". If it is "+", the figure asserts 436 + 24.9 = 17.5, which is false. The line immediately above reads "in-flight = KV budget / KV per request" and the caption says "KV budget / the per-request KV price sets concurrency", so the intent is division; the glyph simply must not be confusable with a plus at print size.
issue.evidence: Rendered PDF p.154 / printed p.134, line "~ 436 GB [op] 24.9 GB = 17.5 -> ~17 requests"; the line above reads "in-flight = KV budget / KV per request"; caption reads "KV budget / the per-request KV price sets concurrency".
issue.acceptance_test: At >=300 dpi the operator is unambiguously a division sign (or the line is rewritten "17.5 = 436 GB / 24.9 GB"); no reader at print size can read it as "+".

issue.issue: The figure title says "640 GB pool" and draws one contiguous bar, which invites the reading that 640 GB is a single freely-allocatable pool. The caption's own aggregate-feasibility caveat says the opposite: 640 GB is an aggregate across eight 80 GB H100s and per-rank fit must be validated separately. The figure carries no rank structure, so the caveat exists only in prose and the figure actively contradicts it.
issue.evidence: PDF p.154 / printed p.134: title "Concurrency budget - one 8xH100 host" with "640 GB pool"; caption "640 GB is an aggregate across eight 80 GB H100s, not a freely-allocatable heap - per-rank fit must be validated separately". Contrast FIG 7.8 (PDF p.155), which does draw the 8 x 80 GB rank structure.
issue.acceptance_test: FIG 7.7 either draws the eight 80 GB rank boundaries (as FIG 7.8 does) or its title/annotation states "aggregate across 8 ranks - not one allocatable pool"; the caption caveat is then visible in the figure, not only in prose.

issue.issue: The caption's central teaching point - "floor 17, not 18" - is asserted rather than shown. issue.figure: FIGURE 8.2 (Per-GPU roofline: dense FP16, one H100 vs one H200)
issue.issue: The two ridge labels appear transposed. As rendered, the blue (H100) curve carries the label "H200 ridge = 295" and the red (H200) curve carries "H100 ridge = 206". The book's own arithmetic gives the opposite: H100 ridge = 989 TFLOPS / 3.35 TB/s = 295 FLOP/byte; H200 ridge = 989 TFLOPS / 4.8 TB/s = 206 FLOP/byte. The body text on the facing page states this explicitly, so a reader who trusts the figure learns the wrong ridge geometry for both GPUs and sees the figure contradict the prose one page earlier.
issue.evidence: PDF p.169 / printed p.149: annotations "H200 ridge = 295" (blue) and "H100 ridge = 206" (red); legend "H100 FP16 (3.35 TB/s)" / "H200 FP16 (4.8 TB/s)"; PDF p.168 / printed p.148 prose: "the ridge point for dense FP16 on H100 is ~295 FLOP/byte (989 / 3.35) and ~206 on H200 (989 / 4.8)". The drawn knees are correct (blue knee right of red knee), so the error is in the labels.
issue.acceptance_test: Rendered figure shows "H100 ridge = 295" in the H100 (blue) colour adjacent to the blue curve's knee and "H200 ridge = 206" in the H200 (red) colour adjacent to the red curve's knee; figure and printed p.148 agree; each label sits within one label-height of its own curve.

issue.issue: The prefill marker does not appear to sit at the arithmetic intensity its own label states. The label reads "prefill 9.2K (intensity ~ 9.2K FLOP/byte)", but on the log x-axis (10^-1 ... 10^4) the vertical dashed prefill line appears to fall between 10^2 and 10^3 (roughly 5 x 10^2 FLOP/byte), not at 9.2 x 10^3, which would place it immediately left of the 10^4 tick. Either the marker or the label is wrong. The qualitative claim (prefill right of the ridge, on the compute-bound plateau) survives either placement, so this is a quantitative error, not a conclusion error.
issue.evidence: PDF p.169 / printed p.149: x-axis ticks 10^-1, 10^0, 10^1, 10^2, 10^3, 10^4; the red dashed vertical line is drawn well left of the 10^4 tick while its annotation states "intensity ~ 9.2K FLOP/byte"; the caption separately says "the plotted prefill (9.2K input) ... points are illustrative operating points".
issue.acceptance_test: At >=300 dpi the vertical dashed prefill line is at log10 = 3.96 (9.2 x 10^3 FLOP/byte), immediately left of the 10^4 tick and clear of the "compute plateau = 989 TFLOPS" annotation; if the plotted intensity is not 9.2K, the label is corrected to the plotted value and the caption's "prefill (9.2K input)" wording is reconciled.

issue.issue: The prefill point's arithmetic intensity is quoted without its denominator. 9.2K FLOP/byte is obtained by dividing prefill FLOPs (1,288 TFLOP) by weight bytes only (140 GB); including the KV write traffic for 9.2K tokens (~24.1 GB) gives ~7.9K FLOP/byte, and including activation traffic lowers it further. The figure's caption insists on separating "a theoretical bound ... from a measured latency", so the denominator belongs in the annotation.
issue.evidence: PDF p.169 / printed p.149: annotation "prefill 9.2K (intensity ~ 9.2K FLOP/byte)"; 1,288 TFLOP / 140 GB = 9,200 FLOP/byte; 1,288 TFLOP / (140 + 24.1) GB ~ 7,850 FLOP/byte.
issue.acceptance_test: The annotation or caption states the denominator ("weights only"), and if the KV-write-inclusive value is used the plotted x-position is updated to match; the reader can reproduce the plotted intensity from the stated inputs.

issue.issue: The "prefill 9.2K (intensity ~ 9.2K FLOP/byte)" annotation appears to overlap the vertical dashed prefill line it labels.
issue.evidence: PDF p.169 / printed p.149: the three-line orange annotation sits across the path of the red dashed vertical line.
issue.acceptance_test: At >=300 dpi the annotation text and the dashed line do not overlap; the label is offset with clear white space.

issue.issue: The denoiser box states "Patch (1, 2), N = 27,280 video tokens". "Patch (1, 2)" is dimensionally incomplete and, read as (T, H), implies a 44 x 40 latent and 18,080 tokens - a 34% error in the figure's headline number.

issue.page: PDF 155 / printed 135; PDF 161 / printed 141; PDF 169 / printed 149; PDF 175 / printed 155
issue.issue: Four of the five figure captions in this batch contain duplicated or garbled clauses - the same sentence fragment appears twice, or a clause is left half-finished. This is one systematic caption-assembly defect, not four independent typos, and it is visible to every reader. Examples as rendered: FIG 7.8 "... the 24.9 GB KV budget of 17.5 -> 17 concurrent (floor 17, not 18: ..." repeated; FIG 8.1 "compute, memory and interconnect are separate bandwidths are distinct architectural constraints" repeated and ungrammatical; FIG 8.2 "a kernel's position on the roofline is a theoretical bound on the roofline - it is not a measured latency" and "host-level attainable performance additional depends on sharding and communication"; FIG 8.3 "For aligned F=4k+1, F_I2V=1+4x(31-1) = 121 latent time positions correspond to frame" and the repeated "not autoregressive text decode" point. FIG 7.7's caption is clean, which is presumably why the defect survived earlier rounds.
issue.evidence: Captions on PDF p.155 / printed p.135 (FIG 7.8), PDF p.161 / printed p.141 (FIG 8.1), PDF p.169 / printed p.149 (FIG 8.2), PDF p.175 / printed p.155 (FIG 8.3). FIG 7.7 (PDF p.154) is clean.
issue.acceptance_test: A duplicate-phrase scan over every figure caption in the book returns zero hits; each caption reads as one clean argument with no repeated clause and no unfinished clause; the four captions above are re-read aloud by a second person before release.

issue.issue: The drawn reduce-scatter outcome is not reachable under the drawn ring direction. The 'Balanced ring neighbor order (both phases)' row shows R0 -> R1 -> R2 -> R3 -> R0, and the note states 'Each rank sends one 2 B chunk to the next rank', i.e. send direction r -> r+1. Yet the reduce-scatter row shows Rank 0 holding [10] (chunk 0), Rank 1 [20] (chunk 1), Rank 2 [-10] (chunk 2), Rank 3 [0] (chunk 3). In a ring reduce-scatter with direction r -> r+1, rank r ends holding chunk (r+1) mod N, so Rank 0 should hold [20], Rank 1 [-10], Rank 2 [0], Rank 3 [10]. The drawn assignment is only reachable if the ring runs r -> r-1, which the arrows contradict.
issue.evidence: Independent re-derivation from the figure's own inputs. Chunk j of rank r = [r+1+j, 2(r+1+j), -(r+1+j), 0]; chunk sums are chunk0=[10,20,-10,0], chunk1=[14,28,-14,0], chunk2=[18,36,-18,0], chunk3=[22,44,-22,0]. Simulating the ring with direction r -> r+1 over 3 rounds: round 0 rank r sends chunk r and receives chunk (r-1); round 1 sends (r-1), receives (r-2); round 2 sends (r-2), receives (r-3). Rank 0 therefore accumulates chunks 3, 2, 1 and ends with chunk 1 = [20]. Cross-checked on N=2 (rank 0 sends chunk 0, receives chunk 1, ends with chunk 1). The figure's byte accounting (6 B sent + 6 B received per rank per phase; 12 B + 12 B per rank total; 3 rounds per phase) is correct and unaffected by this defect.
issue.acceptance_test: In the source, either (a) reverse the drawn ring to R0 -> R3 -> R2 -> R1 -> R0 and relabel the reduce-scatter outputs as Rank 0 [0], Rank 1 [10], Rank 2 [20], Rank 3 [-10], or (b) keep the drawn direction and relabel the reduce-scatter outputs as Rank 0 [20], Rank 1 [-10], Rank 2 [0], Rank 3 [10]. Then add explicit chunk indices (c0..c3) to the reduce-scatter and all-gather rows. Acceptance: a reader can trace chunk c0 from Rank 0's input through the drawn ring to the rank that holds it after reduce-scatter, and the drawn rank labels agree with the drawn arrow direction.

issue.issue: The caption's index notation is internally inconsistent and cannot be checked against the figure. 'r' is defined as a rank index (r = 0...N-1) and then reused as a round index (r = 0...N-2) in the same sentence; 's' is introduced ('indexed reduce-scatter rounds') and never used again; 't' is introduced for all-gather rounds and then not used (the caption switches back to 'r'); 'i' (chunk index) is never defined. The clause 'rank r sends chunk (i-r) mod N and retains chunk i' is also not satisfiable: because rank r sends chunk r in round 0, it accumulates chunks (r-1), (r-2), (r-3) and retains chunk (r+1) mod N, not chunk i.
issue.evidence: Caption as printed: 'Indices are per phase: r = 0...N-1, s = indexed reduce-scatter rounds; t = 0...N-1 all-gather rounds; r = 0...N-2 rank r sends chunk (i-r) mod N and retains chunk i; in round r of the all-gather (r = 0...N-2) rank r sends chunk (i-r) mod N, beginning with its own reduced chunk i.' The figure carries no chunk indices, no round labels and no rank-to-chunk mapping, so none of the caption's index claims is verifiable from the drawing. The all-gather clause is the one correct piece (rank r holds chunk i_r and sends (i_r - t) mod N); the reduce-scatter clause is not.
issue.acceptance_test: Rewrite the index clause with one symbol per role (e.g. q = rank, t = round, j = chunk), state the ring direction explicitly, and either delete 's' and 't' or use them consistently. Acceptance: every symbol is defined exactly once and used; the reduce-scatter and all-gather rules are each checkable against the drawn boxes; and the 'retains chunk' clause matches the drawn rank-to-chunk assignment (see FIG-9.2-01).

issue.figure: Figure 9.1 (Ring traffic and directional bandwidth) — cross-page consistency
issue.issue: The prose's Ethernet option contradicts Figure 9.1's link speed and contains a wrong unit conversion: '35 Gb/s = 3.125 GB/s unidirectional'. 35 Gb/s = 4.375 GB/s; 3.125 GB/s = 25 Gb/s. Figure 9.1's caption and legend label the RoCE curve '25GbE RoCE path' at 2.5 GB/s assumed effective, and the prose's own 2.5 GB/s effective figure is 80% of 3.125 GB/s (25 Gb/s) but only 57% of 4.375 GB/s (35 Gb/s).
issue.evidence: Printed p.168: 'Option C - 35 Gb/s Ethernet (RoCEv2) across 8 nodes. 35 Gb/s = 3.125 GB/s unidirectional.' Printed p.163 (Fig 9.1 caption): '2.5 GB/s for an assumed effective 25GbE RoCE path'; legend: '25GBE RoCE: assumed effective 2.5 GB/s'. Arithmetic: 35/8 = 4.375; 25/8 = 3.125. The 98,000 ms RoCE point in Fig 9.1 is 245 GB / 2.5 GB/s, which is consistent with the 25 Gb/s reading and with the prose's own effective-bandwidth assumption.
issue.acceptance_test: Change '35 Gb/s' to '25 Gb/s' (or, if 35 Gb/s is genuinely intended, change the conversion to 4.375 GB/s and restate the effective-bandwidth assumption and its percentage of line rate). Acceptance: link speed, GB/s conversion, assumed effective bandwidth and Figure 9.1's '25GbE RoCE' legend label all agree, and the 98 s ring time still equals 245 GB / 2.5 GB/s.

issue.issue: The two ring-time displays on printed p.168 do not evaluate to their stated results as rendered, and the symbolic form appears to be missing a factor in each case, so the reader cannot reproduce Figure 9.1's plotted points from the book's own model. Escalate to P1 if the source matches the render. The correct ring all-reduce model is T = 2*(N-1)/N * M / B_eff.
issue.evidence: As rendered at 150 dpi, display 1 reads T_ring ~ (N-1)/N * M / B_eff ~ ... GB / 8.40 GB/s ~ 6.1 s. (N-1)/N * M = 122.5 GB; 122.5/8.40 = 14.6 s, not 6.1 s. The stated 6.1 s equals 245 GB / 40 GB/s = 2*(7/8)*140 GB / 40 GB/s, which is exactly Figure 9.1's HDR point (6,125 ms) - so the symbolic numerator is missing the leading factor 2. Display 2 reads T_ring ~ 2*140 GB / 8 * 2.5 GB/s ~ 98 s; (2*140/8)/2.5 = 14 s and (2*140/8)*2.5 = 87.5 s, neither of which is 98 s; 98 s requires 245 GB / 2.5 GB/s, i.e. the numerator is missing the (N-1) factor (98 = 7 x 14). The prose's ratios ('about 11x the ideal NVLink ring time', 'about 180x') are consistent with 6.1 s and 98 s against Fig 9.1's 544 ms, so the results are right and the displayed algebra is what is suspect. NOT VERIFIED against source: the 150-dpi render is ambiguous for the substituted numerals and for a possible leading '2 *' in display 1.
issue.acceptance_test: Confirm the source text of both displays before editing. Acceptance: each display's symbolic form and its substituted numerals evaluate to the printed result (6.1 s and 98 s) and to the corresponding points in Figure 9.1 (245 GB sent per rank / B_eff); the symbolic form explicitly carries the factor 2 for the two phases and the (N-1)/N factor; and the substituted numerator is legible at print size as 245 GB (or 2*(7/8)*140 GB).

issue.issue: The prose says the multi-rail effective bandwidth is 'referenced in Section 9.2 and Fig 9.1', but the value used (8.40 GB/s) appears in neither location.
issue.evidence: Printed p.168: 'the multi-rail effective bandwidth referenced in Section 9.2 and Fig 9.1'. Section 9.2 (printed p.162) quotes 900/450 GB/s NVLink, 25 GB/s nominal HDR and 2.5 GB/s effective Ethernet; Figure 9.1's three curves are 450, 40 and 2.5 GB/s. 8.40 GB/s occurs in neither.
issue.acceptance_test: Either cite the location where 8.40 GB/s is established, or reword to reference the concept rather than a value. Acceptance: every numeric value in the sentence can be located in the cited section or figure.

issue.issue: The blue NVLink curve is clipped by the 0.1 ms axis floor at the left of the plot, so the drawn line appears to originate at 0.1 ms rather than at its model value, inviting the reader to read a floor value that the model does not produce.
issue.evidence: Model t = 1.75*x/B. At x = 0.01 GB, t = 0.0175/450 s = 0.039 ms, below the plotted floor of 0.1 ms; the curve enters the axes at x ~ 0.026 GB. The rendered line appears to start at the bottom-left corner at 0.1 ms. The orange (0.44 ms) and red (7 ms) curves are inside the axes at x = 0.01, so only the blue curve is affected.
issue.acceptance_test: Either extend the y-axis floor to ~0.01 ms, or annotate the clipped region, or start the x-axis where all three curves are inside the axes. Acceptance: no drawn curve endpoint coincides with an axis limit unless that limit is the model value.

issue.issue: Figure 9.2 uses colour for two different meanings simultaneously - the phase labels ('Reduce-scatter' in orange, 'All-gather' in blue) and the box borders (orange = single reduced element, blue = full four-element vector) - and, unlike Figure 10.1, it carries no grayscale note.
issue.evidence: Rendered page: the four input boxes and the four all-gather result boxes are blue-bordered; the four reduce-scatter result boxes are orange-bordered; the phase labels are coloured by phase, not by box state. In grayscale the two borders differ only in lightness, so the phase/state distinction rests on a subtle tonal difference at small type size. Figure 10.1 (PDF 198) explicitly states that its colour key is 'redundant, not load-bearing'; Figure 9.2 makes no equivalent statement.

Acceptance: a grayscale print of the figure can be read without relying on border colour.

issue.figure: Figure 9.3 — 'The payload path is not the bootstrap path'
issue.issue: Within Figure 9.3 the last line of several boxes appears to be set smaller than the lines above it, creating an unintended hierarchy inside a single box and pushing the smallest in-figure type toward the book's 8 pt annotation floor.

issue.issue: Figure 9.3's two columns are never identified by vendor, and the figure's title makes a claim (bootstrap vs payload) that the dominant visual structure (two parallel vendor stacks) does not carry. Separately, both the caption's MPI caveat and the figure's own note concern MPI, which appears in no box on the payload path.

The title 'The payload path is not the bootstrap path' is carried solely by the dashed red control arrows at the top, while the dominant structure is a two-column vendor comparison. Caption: 'Dashed setup connections do not imply that MPI carries the collective payload; GPU-aware MPI can also provide a possible payload implementation.' issue.figure: Figure 10.1 — 'Three parallelism patterns, one per panel', Panel C

issue.issue: Panel B's caption and note describe two things the panel does not draw: the layer stack that is being split, and the idle bubble at fill/drain. The reader is asked to accept the chapter's central claim about pipeline bubbles on the strength of a sentence rather than a picture.

issue.issue: Panel A's communication note understates the collective traffic of tensor parallelism, and the panel does not show the replicated activations that the surrounding prose says are replicated. A reader could infer that TP replicates weights and communicates once per layer.

In a standard transformer block with column/row-parallel projections, TP requires an all-reduce (or reduce-scatter + all-gather) at each row-parallel projection output - typically two per block (attention output projection and MLP down-projection) - plus an all-gather for the column-parallel input, so 'every layer' understates the per-block collective count by roughly 2x. The prose below the figure states 'activations are replicated', but Panel A draws only the weight bar and the all-reduce arrow, so nothing in the panel shows what is replicated. Acceptance: the panel's communication note matches the collective count used elsewhere in the book, and the panel shows or names what is replicated.

issue.evidence: Panel (a) 'Avg prefix reuse' and panel (b) 'Decode batch size' show tick labels '1' and '10' only, with the axis running to ~15-16; the spacing of the '10' label is consistent with a linear scale, so the plotted markers at r = 2, 3, 5 and batch 2, 3, 5 are unlabelled.

issue.issue: The caption contains a garbled token where a symbol is expected: 'so x = no sharing and hence no prefix reduction'.
issue.evidence: Caption text: 'average prefill reuse = mean number of requests served from each cached prefix block, so x = no sharing and hence no prefix reduction'. The intended statement is presumably 'r = 1 = no sharing' (or 'zero sharing').
issue.acceptance_test: Inspect the source string and replace the stray glyph with the intended symbol; confirm the caption reads as a complete clause.

issue.issue: The prose that describes Fig 16.1 lists three figure features that are not present in the rendered figure, so the reader's map of the figure is wrong before they reach it.
issue.evidence: Printed p. 282: 'The figure marks the canonical-price point (star) and the full sensitivity span (horizontal line), annotates the feasible bound (24.96M = 40 rps x 624,000 active s), and shades the infeasible region beyond it.' In the rendered Fig 16.1 the canonical point is a green diamond (legend: 'cloud $87.6K/mo @ 6.24M (occupancy input)'), not a star; the sensitivity span appears only as the red text 'sensitivity = 6.2-10.4M' inside an annotation box, with no horizontal line; and the feasible bound is labelled 'feasible max 24.96M' with no derivation. Only the hatched infeasible region matches the prose.
issue.acceptance_test: Reconcile prose and figure: either add the star marker, the horizontal sensitivity-span segment and the '24.96M = 40 rps x 624,000 active s' derivation to Fig 16.1, or rewrite the printed p. 282 sentence to name only the features the figure actually contains (green diamond, red price band, dashed managed line, feasible-max label, hatched region).

issue.issue: The managed $20.8/1K line - the line that defines the ~7.5M break-even the caption highlights - is drawn inside the $15-25/1K band in the same hue, so it is not separable, and in grayscale it collapses into the band.
issue.evidence: At the canonical 6.24M req/mo the band spans $93.6K-$156K and the managed line sits at $129.8K, i.e. strictly inside the band; both are rendered in the red/salmon family. In grayscale the band and the dashed managed line fall at nearly the same tone, so the reader cannot locate the crossing with the blue $155.8K/mo self-host line that the caption calls the break-even.
issue.acceptance_test: Render the figure in grayscale and confirm the managed line is separable from the band (distinct dash pattern, heavier weight, or a leader/label at the crossing); alternatively annotate the crossing point directly on the plot.

issue.issue: The vertical dotted line carrying the 'feasible max 24.96M' label appears to be drawn near the canonical 6.24M marker rather than at the feasible bound, so the label may be attached to the wrong line.
issue.evidence: The figure contains exactly one vertical dotted line. 24.96M should sit at ~85% of the log x-axis (log10 2.496e7 = 7.40 within the 4->8 range) and coincide with the left edge of the hatched INFEASIBLE region; 6.24M sits at ~70% (log10 6.24e6 = 6.80). As rendered, the dotted line appears to fall essentially on the green diamond at 6.24M, while the hatched boundary sits further right.
issue.acceptance_test: In the source, assert that the dotted line's x data value equals 2.496e7 and that it coincides with the hatched region's left edge; re-render and confirm the 'feasible max 24.96M' label sits directly above that line and that the canonical 6.24M marker is not conflated with it.

issue.issue: Legend, annotation-box and axis text appear below the 8 pt print floor for figure annotations.
issue.evidence: The red 'break-even ~ 7.5M / sensitivity = 6.2-10.4M / canonical 6.24M req/mo' box, the green 'cloud $87.6K/mo (occupancy input) / priced at 6.24M req/mo only' box, the four-entry legend and the axis titles all render at a small size, visibly below the body text on the same page and below the 8 pt figure-annotation floor.
issue.acceptance_test: Set legend, annotation and axis text to >= 8 pt; verify the rendered glyph height at 300 dpi and confirm the two annotation boxes remain inside the axes without overlapping the band.

issue.issue: Fig 16.1 appears seven printed pages after the first substantive discussion of its content, and the reader is asked to reason about 'the shape of the cost functions' and the shaded region (printed pp. 278-279) before seeing the figure.
issue.evidence: Printed p. 279: 'the canonical 6.24M-active/s-mo duty cycle are drawn only to show the shape of the cost functions; Fig 16.1 shades and labels that region'. Printed p. 281 carries only a pointer ('Note 16.1 - (Fig 16.1) - line definitions and the cloud marker'). The figure itself is on printed p. 286.
issue.acceptance_test: Move Fig 16.1 to printed p. 279-281 (immediately after the first discussion) or add an explicit 'see Fig 16.1, printed p. 286' pointer at the first mention; confirm the figure is not more than two pages from its first substantive discussion.

issue.figure: Figure 17.1 'Sizing a fleet of one model'
issue.issue: Two annotation strings are drawn on top of each other in the upper-left of the plot area, making both partly illegible.
issue.evidence: Around x = 0.3-4.5 h, y ~ 8.5-9.5 req/s the blue label 'N = 4 fleet (3 working + 1 reserve, ~8.0, ideal)' is superimposed with a second string containing '...N-1 reserve so y still clear it after one host drains: N_provisioned = (8.0 - 5.5) / (1.4 - 0.917) = 3 residual hosts (not a measured load curve)'. The superposition produces an unreadable jumble where the N-1 derivation - the figure's only sizing derivation - should be.
issue.acceptance_test: Re-lay the annotations so no two text objects overlap (e.g. move the N-1 derivation into the top-right box or into the caption); confirm in the rendered PDF that no glyph pairs intersect and that the N-1 derivation is fully legible.

issue.issue: The caption contains a verbatim splice of the figure's internal annotation, producing an ungrammatical caption and duplicating in-figure text.
issue.evidence: Caption: '...so a 3-host fleet (3x0.9 req/s) is sized above it; 3 hosts clear the 5.5 req/s burst at p = 1.4h is the N-1 reserve so y still clear it after one host drains: N_provisioned = (8.0 - 5.5) / (1.4 - 0.917) = 3 residual hosts (not a measured load curve). Burst profile: ...'. The clause from 'at p = 1.4h' through '(not a measured load curve)' is the figure's internal annotation pasted into the caption mid-sentence; the caption then separately states 'Burst profile: the burst curve is an illustrative Gaussian-shaped profile, not a measured load curve', duplicating the same disclaimer.
issue.acceptance_test: Rewrite the caption as continuous prose that states the conclusion (3 hosts x 2.0 req/s = 6.0 req/s at p = 1 clears the 5.5 req/s burst; break-even p = 0.917) and delete the spliced fragment; confirm no caption sentence duplicates an in-figure annotation verbatim.

issue.issue: The printed derivation does not evaluate to its stated result and is dimensionally incoherent: 'N_provisioned = (8.0 - 5.5) / (1.4 - 0.917) = 3 residual hosts'.
issue.evidence: 2.5 / 0.483 = 5.18, not 3. The denominator also mixes a duration (1.4 h) with a dimensionless factor (0.917), so the expression has no consistent unit. The figure's own break-even p = 0.917 is exactly 5.5 / (3 x 2.0) = 0.9167, and the caption's 'at p = 0.85 it is 3 x 0.85 = 2.55 req/s' uses the same missing per-host factor, so the intended derivation is almost certainly N = 5.5 / (2.0 p) = 3 at p = 0.917 (equivalently p_break-even = 5.5 / 6.0). A reader who copies the printed expression over-provisions by ~73%.
issue.acceptance_test: Replace the printed expression with 'p_break-even = 5.5 / (3 x 2.0) = 0.917' (or 'N = 5.5 / (2.0 p) = 3 at p = 0.917'); confirm the printed expression evaluates to the printed result and that all quantities in it share a unit.

issue.issue: The caption's capacity arithmetic omits the ~2.0 req/s per-host capacity, so one parenthetical contradicts the sentence it supports and another understates the fleet capacity by 2x.
issue.evidence: Caption: 'so a 3-host fleet (3x0.9 req/s) is sized above it' - 3 x 0.9 = 2.7 req/s, which is below the 5.5 req/s burst the sentence claims it exceeds, and contradicts the figure's own 'one host ~2.0 req/s' and the orange N-1 residual line at 6.0 req/s. Later: 'at p = 0.85 it is 3 x 0.85 = 2.55 req/s' - the per-host 2.0 req/s factor is missing; the correct value is 3 x 2.0 x 0.85 = 5.1 req/s (still below 5.5, so the conclusion survives).
issue.acceptance_test: Rewrite both parentheticals with the per-host factor included ('3 x 2.0 = 6.0 req/s at p = 1'; '3 x 2.0 x 0.85 = 5.1 req/s'); confirm every capacity number in the caption can be reproduced from the figure's own 2.0 req/s per-host bound.

issue.figure: Figure 17.1 caption vs plotted N-1 residual line
issue.issue: The caption's N-1 residual value conflicts with the figure's plotted residual line and with its own stated margin.
issue.evidence: Caption: 'at ideal p = 1 the N-1 residual = 3 request (~6.6 req/s) clears ~5.5 req/s burst with ~0.5 req/s margin'. The figure's orange 'N = 1 residual (1 host drains, ideal)' line is at 6.0 req/s (3 hosts x 2.0), and 6.0 - 5.5 = 0.5 matches the stated margin, whereas 6.6 - 5.5 = 1.1 does not. '3 request' is also ungrammatical.
issue.acceptance_test: Change the parenthetical to '~6.0 req/s' (or, if 6.6 is intended, redraw the residual line and restate the margin); fix '3 request' -> '3 requests'.

issue.issue: Legend/plot mismatch: the legend lists two orange entries with different dash patterns, but the plot contains only one orange line and no line at 2.0 req/s, so the plotted dashed line matches the wrong legend sample.
issue.evidence: Legend entries: 'offered load (burst)' (red solid), 'N = 4 fleet capacity (~8.0, ideal)' (blue solid), 'one host burst (~2.0, ideal)' (orange dashed), 'N = 1 residual (1 host drains, ideal)' (orange dotted). The plot contains a blue solid line at 8.0 and one orange dashed line at 6.0; there is no line at 2.0 req/s and no orange dotted line. The in-plot text 'one host cannot meet load above ~2.0 req/s' asserts a bound the figure never draws.
issue.acceptance_test: Either draw the single-host 2.0 req/s reference line and keep both legend entries, or delete the 'one host burst' entry and make the residual line's dash pattern match its legend sample; confirm every legend sample maps to exactly one plotted line.

issue.issue: The black label 'one host ~2.0 req/s' at the right of the plot lies on the descending red burst curve.
issue.evidence: The label sits at roughly x = 8.5-10.5 h, y ~ 2.4 req/s; over that x-range the red curve falls from ~2.8 to ~2.2 req/s, so the curve stroke passes through the glyphs.
issue.acceptance_test: Move the label clear of the curve (e.g. below the curve or with a short leader) and confirm in the rendered PDF that no curve stroke intersects the label glyphs.

issue.issue: The annotation sentence is garbled: a subject token is missing, a dimensionless factor is written with a time unit, and one clause is not a sentence.
issue.evidence: Box text: 'ideal p = 1 analytical ceiling - no SLO claim. N-1 clears the burst only for p ~ 0.917: req/s burst at p = 1.4h is the N-1 reserve so y still clear it after one host drains: N_provisioned = ...'. The subject ('the 5.5') is missing before 'req/s burst'; 'p = 1.4h' mixes a dimensionless factor with a duration (the burst peak is at t ~ 5.4 h on the x-axis); 'so y still clear it' is not a clause.
issue.acceptance_test: Rewrite as: 'N-1 clears the burst only for p >= 0.917: the 5.5 req/s burst at t ~ 5.4 h is covered by the 3-host residual (6.0 req/s at p = 1)'; confirm every symbol in the box is defined and dimensionally consistent.

issue.issue: Dangling clause in the caption: '...at p = 0.85 it is 3 x 0.85 = 2.55 req/s, so the 5.5 burst - so the 6.0 rps residual is not a robust failover margin...'.
issue.evidence: The fragment 'so the 5.5 burst -' has no predicate and is followed by a second 'so', leaving the sentence without a main clause.
issue.acceptance_test: Complete or delete the fragment; read the caption aloud for grammatical continuity after the FIG-310-04 rewrite.

issue.issue: The in-panel annotation and the legend state two mutually inconsistent values for the same quantity. The orange annotation reads 'generated y = 0.05x output (q = 300)', which yields y = 15 tokens, while the legend below panel (a) reads 'generated (y=65)'. Neither 0.05x300 = 15 nor 65/300 = 0.217 is consistent with the other. A reader sizing KV from this figure cannot tell which value is authoritative.
issue.evidence: Independent rederivation from the figure's own numbers: the legend's y = 65 is the value that reconciles with panel (b). Per-turn increment = retrieved 800 + generated 65 = 865 tokens; at the book's canonical 2.62 MB/token FP16 KV that is 865 x 2.62 = 2,266 MB = 2.27 GB/turn. Series: single-shot 9,500 tok -> 24.89 GB (printed 24.9); T1 10,365 -> 27.16 GB (printed 27.2); T2 11,230 -> 29.42 GB (printed 29.4); T3 12,095 -> 31.69 GB (printed 31.7); T4 12,960 -> 33.96 GB (printed 34.0). All five printed bars reproduce exactly with y = 65 and fail with y = 15 (which would give T4 = 12,760 tok -> 33.4 GB, contradicting the printed 34.0 and the caption's '~34.0 GB'). The caption on printed p. 342 independently states 12,960 tokens x 2.62 MB/token = 34.0 GB. Therefore the annotation's coefficient (or its parenthetical) is the defective element, not the legend.
issue.acceptance_test: Exactly one of the two statements survives. Either (a) the annotation is rewritten to state the rule that actually produces 65 (e.g. 'generated y = 65 tokens/turn (0.217 x output)'), or (b) the legend and panel (b) are regenerated from a corrected y. Acceptance: a reader can derive every one of the five panel (b) bar labels (24.9, 27.2, 29.4, 31.7, 34.0 GB) from the legend values and the 2.62 MB/token constant stated in the caption, with no residual contradiction.

issue.issue: The decision tree has an orphaned leaf: the green 'Small gen' box has no incoming edge and no condition attached to it. The capability-filter bracket feeds Embedding / Vision / Math-reason; the cost/SLO gate feeds Frontier only; Fallthrough feeds General only. The caption nevertheless claims the figure shows 'the specialist, frontier/small and general-purpose model families as leaves', so the figure does not depict what the caption says it depicts, and the reader cannot infer under what condition a small general model is selected.
issue.evidence: Rendered page inspection: three downward connectors exist in the leaf row (one bracket to the three blue boxes, one to 'Frontier', one to 'General'). No connector terminates on 'Small gen'. The caption's own leaf list names 'frontier/small' as a pair, implying Frontier and Small gen are siblings under the cost/SLO gate's 'yes' branch.
issue.acceptance_test: Every leaf box has exactly one incoming edge carrying a legible condition, and the caption's leaf list matches the drawn leaves one-for-one. Specifically: either the cost/SLO gate's 'yes' edge fans out to Frontier and Small gen with the selection rule stated (e.g. 'yes -> size tier: frontier if SLO requires, else small gen'), or 'Small gen' is removed from the figure and from the caption's leaf list. Acceptance: no box in the leaf row is reachable only by color.

issue.issue: The color legend is incomplete and overloaded. It reads 'color: blue = specialist . teal = frontier . green = small gen . purple = general-purpose' but omits the amber fill used for the three decision nodes (Capability filter, Cost/SLO gate, Fallthrough), and the 'Request' box is filled with the same blue the legend assigns to 'specialist'. A reader applying the legend literally classifies the request as a specialist model.
issue.evidence: Rendered page inspection: 'Request' and 'Embedding'/'Vision'/'Math-reason' share the same blue fill and white bold type; the legend's blue key is labelled 'specialist'. The amber fill of the three decision nodes has no key entry.
issue.acceptance_test: The legend enumerates every fill class used in the figure (including the decision-node class and the request/source class), and no box's fill is ambiguous under the legend. Acceptance: a reader can classify all 10 boxes in the figure using the legend alone, with no class unassigned and no class assigned to two different meanings.

issue.issue: White bold text on the amber decision-node fills (Capability filter, Cost/SLO gate, Fallthrough) is the weakest text in the figure once the page is printed in grayscale. The amber appears to be a mid-light orange (approximately #E8A33D), whose grayscale luminance is roughly 67%, giving white-on-amber a contrast ratio near 2.3:1 - below the 3:1 large-text threshold and far below 4.5:1. The three boxes that carry the entire routing logic become the least legible elements on the page.
issue.evidence: Rendered page inspection: the three amber boxes carry white bold labels; the blue, teal and purple boxes are substantially darker in luminance and survive grayscale conversion. The amber class is also the one with no legend entry (FIG-18.1-02), so the reader cannot fall back on the legend to disambiguate.
issue.acceptance_test: Convert the page to grayscale and measure the text/background contrast for every label in the figure; all labels must reach at least 4.5:1 (or 3:1 for bold >=14pt). Acceptance: either the amber fill is darkened to a luminance that supports white text, or the decision-node labels are set in a dark ink on the amber fill.

issue.issue: The 'resolved' connector and its label are visually ambiguous against the dashed return path. The word 'resolved' sits in the narrow band between the dashed 'loop (iterate) - not resolved' horizontal run and the 'limit hit' arrow, immediately beneath the word 'not resolved' in that dashed-path label, and the Decide -> 'Final answer' elbow is routed within a few points of the dashed path. A reader can plausibly pair the label 'resolved' with the dashed return path whose own label says 'not resolved'.
issue.evidence: Rendered page inspection at 150 dpi: the dashed return path runs horizontally from Decide back to Plan at a height that passes directly above the 'resolved' text; the 'resolved' text sits below that dashed line and immediately left of the vertical 'limit hit' arrow; the 'Final answer' box is offset far to the left of Decide, forcing an elbow whose horizontal segment runs parallel to and just below the dashed line.
issue.acceptance_test: Re-route so that the three exits from Decide are unambiguous: place 'Final answer' directly beneath 'Decide', or route the resolved edge on a path separated from the dashed return by at least 12 pt, and place the 'resolved' label on its own connector segment. Acceptance: at 150 dpi no reader pairs 'resolved' with the dashed path, and the word 'resolved' and the phrase 'not resolved' do not appear within one line-height of each other.

issue.issue: The caption's evidence label mixes the book's two provenance/status axes: 'Assumption: status [ILLUSTRATIVE]'. Under the book's own convention (Ch 4 and the Appendix A axis table), [ILLUSTRATIVE] is a provenance label and [ASSUMPTION] is a status label; the caption places a provenance label in the status slot. The same book uses the correct two-label form for FIG 18.1 ('[ILLUSTRATIVE conceptual] [DERIVED]'), so the figure-caption label syntax is also internally inconsistent.
issue.evidence: Rendered page inspection: FIG 19.1 caption reads 'Assumption: status [ILLUSTRATIVE]'; FIG 18.1 caption (PDF 348 / printed 328) reads '[ILLUSTRATIVE conceptual] [DERIVED]'; FIG 19.2 caption (PDF 363 / printed 343) reads '[DERIVED]'. Three different syntaxes for the same mechanism across three consecutive figure captions.
issue.acceptance_test: All figure captions use one syntax: provenance label first, status label second, drawn from the book's defined sets. Acceptance: FIG 19.1's label reads '[ILLUSTRATIVE] [ASSUMPTION]' (or whichever pair is intended), and a grep of all figure captions returns a single consistent pattern.

issue.issue: Panel (a)'s axis is titled 'Tokens / request' and the panel is titled 'Tokens accumulate', but the bars are retained context, not processed tokens - a distinction that appears only as a sentence in the caption. The adjacent prose on printed p. 342 quotes 41,990 prefill tokens at T=3 while panel (a)'s T=3 bar is ~12,095 tokens, a 3.5x discrepancy that a reader who has not read the caption note will read as a contradiction between figure and text.
issue.evidence: Rendered page inspection: panel (a) y-axis label 'Tokens / request', panel title 'Tokens accumulate'; the caption's only reconciliation is 'Bars are RETAINED context/KV, not summed per-call processed or billed tokens.' Printed p. 342 (PDF 362) states 'the prefill/decode token ratio rises from 30.7 (9,200 / 300) single-shot to 84.8 (41,990 / 495) at T=3'. The figure's own caption says 'four turns take a request from ~24.9 GB KV to ~34.0 GB of KV', i.e. 12,960 tokens at T=4, confirming the figure is on the retained-context basis.
issue.acceptance_test: The axis itself carries the distinction, not only the caption. Acceptance: panel (a)'s y-axis reads 'retained context tokens / request' (or the panel title is changed to 'Retained context accumulates'), and a reader who reads only the figure and printed p. 342 can reconcile 12,095 vs 41,990 without consulting the caption.

issue.issue: The annotation 'generated y = 0.05x output (q = 300)' is set in a light orange on the white plot background. That fill has a contrast ratio of roughly 1.4-1.5:1 against white, so the annotation is effectively illegible in grayscale and marginal even in color - and it is the annotation that carries the (currently wrong) rule for the generated segment.
issue.evidence: Rendered page inspection: the annotation is the only orange text on a white field in the figure; the panel (b) value labels use a dark red that survives grayscale comfortably. The same orange is used as a fill in the legend swatch, where it is legible because it is a solid block rather than thin text.
issue.acceptance_test: Measure the annotation's text/background contrast in grayscale; it must reach at least 4.5:1. Acceptance: the annotation is set in a text-safe color (or on a filled callout box with a dark ink), and remains readable in a grayscale print of the page.

issue.issue: The cost/SLO gate's affirmative edge label is a four-line stack ('yes ->' / 'SLO:' / 'frontier' / 'cost: small') that mixes a branch condition with an unexplained rationale. The reader cannot tell whether 'frontier cost: small' is a condition the gate tests, a note about the frontier tier, or a restatement of the gate's name. The stack also sits in the same vertical band as the adjacent 'yes -> specialist family (one selected)' label, crowding the two branch annotations.
issue.evidence: Rendered page inspection: the label occupies roughly four short lines immediately left of the gate's downward arrow, with the specialist-branch label ending only a few points to its left.
issue.acceptance_test: The affirmative edge carries a single-line condition naming the selection rule (e.g. 'yes -> size tier: frontier if SLO requires, else small gen'), with any rationale moved to the caption. Acceptance: the label is one line, and the two 'yes' branch labels are separated by at least one line-height of clear space.

issue.issue: The Fallthrough -> General edge is labeled 'no match -> general', but 'no match' has already been consumed by the capability filter's 'no' branch, which routes to the cost/SLO gate rather than to General. The same phrase therefore denotes two different conditions in one diagram, and the reader may conclude that a capability-filter miss bypasses the cost/SLO gate.
issue.evidence: Rendered page inspection: the capability filter's outgoing edges are 'no' (-> Cost/SLO gate) and 'yes -> specialist family'; the Fallthrough -> General edge is the only place 'no match' appears.
issue.acceptance_test: Each edge label names a distinct condition. Acceptance: the Fallthrough -> General edge reads e.g. 'no tier passed -> general', and no condition phrase appears on two edges with different meanings.

issue.issue: Caption grammar error: 'Each specialist model (Embedding/Vision/Math) is a leaf of the router can dispatch to.' The relative clause is malformed.
issue.evidence: Rendered page inspection of the caption block under FIGURE 18.1.
issue.acceptance_test: Reads 'is a leaf the router can dispatch to' (or 'is one of the leaves the router can dispatch to').

issue.issue: The caption applies the status label [DERIVED] to a figure that contains no derived quantity - no rates, no thresholds, no arithmetic. The caption itself defers the numbers ('the tiers, rates and thresholds themselves are in SS18.3.1-SS18.3.4'), so the status label has no referent in the figure.
issue.evidence: Rendered page inspection: FIG 18.1 contains only box labels, edge labels and a color legend; no numeric value appears anywhere in the drawing.
issue.acceptance_test: The caption's status label names the status of something the figure actually contains. Acceptance: either the status label is dropped (leaving the provenance label), or the caption states in one clause what is derived (e.g. 'the decision order is derived from the SS18.3.1-SS18.3.4 worked example').

issue.issue: The caption's central distinction - 'a turn/to-kernel budget check - not the model's judgment - ends the loop at the limit' - is not visible in the drawing. 'limit hit' leaves the same 'Decide / check / resolved?' box as the model's own resolution, so the figure alone supports the reading the caption explicitly rejects (that the model decides to stop at the limit).
issue.evidence: Rendered page inspection: the Decide box carries the sub-labels 'check' and 'resolved?', and two downward edges leave it ('resolved' to Final answer, 'limit hit' to Stopped) with no visual distinction between a model decision and a harness-enforced stop.
issue.acceptance_test: The figure distinguishes the two checks. Acceptance: the limit edge is labeled to name its source (e.g. 'limit hit (harness budget exhausted)') or the Decide box is split into 'model resolved?' and 'budget exhausted?', so the caption's claim is readable from the drawing alone.

issue.issue: The caption phrase 'a turn/to-kernel budget check' uses 'to-kernel', which is not a term defined or used anywhere else in the manuscript and reads as a typo for 'token'. A reader encountering it in a caption that is otherwise precise will stop to parse it.
issue.evidence: Rendered page inspection of the FIGURE 19.1 caption; the book's established vocabulary is 'turn' and 'token' (e.g. 'turn-count distribution', 'tokens per request').
issue.acceptance_test: The phrase reads 'a turn/token budget check' (or the intended term is defined in the glossary and used consistently).

issue.issue: The small italic role labels inside the state boxes ('model', 'action', 'state', 'check' on the pale-blue row; 'emit', 'done', 'limit', 'terminal' on the amber row) are the smallest and faintest text in the figure. The blue-on-pale-blue role labels sit near a 4:1 grayscale contrast and the brown-on-amber role labels are lower still, so at print size the role annotations - which carry the state-machine semantics - are the first thing to disappear.
issue.evidence: Rendered page inspection: the role labels are set in a lighter, italic face than the box titles and are visibly lower-contrast than the box titles in both panels of the figure.
issue.acceptance_test: All in-box annotation text reaches at least 4.5:1 in grayscale at final print size. Acceptance: role labels are set in the same dark ink as the box titles (or in a dedicated dark accent), and remain legible in a grayscale print.

issue.issue: The orange annotation is placed inside the plot area at a height that coincides with the upper portion of the tallest bars, so the text and the bar tops compete for the same band. At 150 dpi the annotation is visually crowded with the turn-3/turn-4 bar tops rather than sitting in clear space.
issue.evidence: Rendered page inspection: the annotation occupies the upper-left of panel (a)'s axes, at a vertical position comparable to the tops of the right-hand bars; panel (a)'s y-axis extends to 14,000, leaving headroom above the tallest bar (~12,960) that the annotation does not use.
issue.acceptance_test: No glyph in the annotation intersects or touches bar geometry at 300 dpi. Acceptance: the annotation is moved above the axes or into the empty upper-left region, and a 300-dpi render shows clear separation between the annotation and every bar.

issue.issue: Panel (a) has no x-axis title while panel (b) is titled 'Agent turns', even though the two panels share the same category axis ((single-shot), 1, 2, 3, 4). The reader must infer the shared axis from the tick labels alone.
issue.evidence: Rendered page inspection: panel (b) carries the centered x-axis label 'Agent turns'; panel (a) has only the category tick labels.
issue.acceptance_test: Either both panels carry 'Agent turns' or the figure uses a single shared x-axis label centered under the pair.

issue.issue: Panel (a)'s y-axis tick labels are unseparated thousands ('2000', '4000', ... '14000'), inconsistent with the book's comma-separated thousands used everywhere else in the text and in the figure's own caption ('9,200', '12,960', '24.9 GB').
issue.evidence: Rendered page inspection: panel (a) y-axis reads 0, 2000, 4000, 6000, 8000, 10000, 12000, 14000; the caption on the same page writes '9,200-token prompt' and '~24.9 GB'.
issue.acceptance_test: Panel (a)'s ticks are formatted 2,000 / 4,000 / ... / 14,000, matching the book's number formatting.

issue.page: PDF 363 / printed 343 (caption) and PDF 362 / printed 342 (adjacent prose)
issue.issue: The caption and the adjacent prose give the reader two different numbers for the same effect and the prose's framing contradicts the caption. The caption says four turns take a request 'from ~24.9 GB KV to ~34.0 GB of KV - 36% jump'; the prose one page earlier says the same move 'is not a "35% GPU memory" tweak but a move from ~24.9 GB KV per request ... to ~34.0 GB KV per request'. The move the prose dismisses as a 35% tweak is the move the caption quantifies as 36%.
issue.evidence: Independent recomputation: (33.955 - 24.890) / 24.890 = 36.4%, so the caption's 36% is correct on unrounded values; the prose's '35%' is the same quantity rounded differently and is used rhetorically to deny that the effect is small. The prose never states what the fleet-level amplification actually is, which is the point it appears to be making.
issue.acceptance_test: The two numbers are reconciled in one voice. Acceptance: the prose states the per-request KV growth (36%) and then states the fleet-level amplification explicitly (e.g. the reduction in concurrent slots per host at fixed KV capacity), so the caption's '36% jump' and the prose's claim support each other rather than appearing to contradict.

issue.issue: The caption sentence 'Caveat: a production stack that can hold this flat, prefix-cache reduces recomputation and shares prefix KV but does not by itself reduce the request's KV-resident context' uses 'hold this flat' without an antecedent the reader can resolve - flat context, flat memory, flat allocation? The sentence is doing real work (it is the figure's only caveat about production reality) and is currently opaque.
issue.evidence: Rendered page inspection of the FIGURE 19.2 caption; 'flat' is not used elsewhere in the chapter in this sense.
issue.acceptance_test: The caveat is rewritten so that 'flat' has an explicit referent (e.g. 'a production stack that can hold the accumulated context flat, i.e. without evicting or compacting it'), or the word is replaced with a precise one.

issue.figure: Figure 22.1 (Attention vs. projection prefill FLOP crossover), left panel annotation + caption
issue.issue: The annotation 'full-square quad overtakes ~52.4K' and the caption's 'at ~52.4K context tokens under full-square counting' are numerically wrong. The correct crossover is ~53.4K. The figure contradicts itself: its own legend defines the full-square quadratic term as 4*n_layers*L^2*d and the causal-triangle term as 2*n_layers*L^2*d, i.e. exactly a factor of two, so the two crossover points against the same linear term MUST differ by exactly a factor of two. The figure prints 106.8K for the causal case (correct) and 52.4K for the full-square case (should be 53.4K). This is a digit transposition (53.4 -> 52.4), not a modelling difference.
issue.evidence: Independent rederivation from the figure's own stated geometry (caption: 70B, 80 layers, hidden d=8192) and the figure's own legend formulas: linear(L) = 2*N*L = 2*70e9*L = 1.4e11*L. Full-square quad(L) = 4*80*8192*L^2 = 2,621,440*L^2. Setting quad = linear: L = 1.4e11 / 2,621,440 = 53,406.6 tokens = 53.4K. Causal quad(L) = 2*80*8192*L^2 = 1,310,720*L^2; L = 1.4e11 / 1,310,720 = 106,813 = 106.8K, which reproduces the figure's printed causal value exactly and therefore confirms N=70e9, n_layers=80, d=8192 are the intended constants. Cross-check: 106,813/2 = 53,406. The printed 52.4K is inconsistent with the printed 106.8K by a factor of 2.038, not 2. The conclusion ('at 32K it is large but not yet dominant') is unaffected: at L=32,000, quad/linear = 2,621,440*32,000/1.4e11 = 0.599, so the qualitative statement still holds; the defect is the wrong number, not the wrong conclusion. NOT VERIFIED against the source file (no tool access); the rederivation above is deterministic from the printed figure and caption.
issue.acceptance_test: A deterministic rederivation from N=70e9, n_layers=80, d=8192 must print 53,406 tokens (53.4K) for the full-square crossover and 106,813 tokens (106.8K) for the causal crossover; the figure annotation and the caption must both read '~53.4K'. The two printed values must satisfy full_square_crossover * 2 == causal_crossover to within rounding.

issue.issue: The annotation 'causal-triangle quad overtakes linear ~106.8K' points at a crossing that is outside the plotted x-range. The x-axis spans 10^0 to 10^2 in K tokens (1K to 100K), and at the right edge (100K) the causal-triangle quadratic term (1.31e16) is still BELOW the linear term (1.40e16). The reader is directed to a feature the figure does not contain, and the leader line terminates at the plot boundary rather than at a crossing.
issue.evidence: quad_causal(100,000) = 2*80*8192*(1e5)^2 = 1.31072e16 FLOP; linear(100,000) = 2*70e9*1e5 = 1.4e16 FLOP. Ratio 0.937 < 1, so no crossing occurs within the axis. The crossing is at 106,813 tokens (see FIG-22.1-01 derivation), i.e. 6.8% beyond the right edge. The same applies to the 'total (causal-triangle)' orange dotted curve, which crosses the linear term at the same point. The full-square crossing (53.4K) IS in range, so the figure is asymmetric in a way the reader will not notice.
issue.acceptance_test: Either extend the left panel's x-axis to at least 3e2 K tokens so both annotated crossings are visible, or replace the off-scale annotation with an explicit off-scale marker (e.g. an arrow to the right edge labelled 'crossing at 106.8K, beyond axis') plus a note that the causal-triangle curve has not yet overtaken the linear term at 100K. A reviewer must be able to locate both annotated crossings inside the axes.

issue.issue: The log-axis tick exponents are the most consequential labels in the figure and they are not legible at print size in the rendered page. As rendered, the left panel's y-axis appears to read 10^-1 / 10^0 / 10^1 / 10^2 and the right panel's 10^-1 / 10^-2 / 10^-3 / 10^-4 / 10^-5, which would contradict the axis titles 'Prefill compute (FLOP / request)' and 'Decode compute (FLOP / token)' by 10^15 and 10^11 respectively (prefill at the canonical 9.2K is ~1.5e15 FLOP; decode 2N is 1.4e11 FLOP/token). The most likely truth is that the ticks are raw FLOP (10^14-10^17 left, 10^8-10^12 right), but this cannot be confirmed from the rendered page, and a reader who misreads them will conclude the figure is off by fifteen orders of magnitude.
issue.evidence: Left panel geometry is unit-invariant (the curves occupy identical relative positions under either reading), so the tick glyphs are the only discriminator and they are sub-legible at the rendered resolution. Right panel: 2N = 2*70e9 = 1.4e11 FLOP/token; under a 10^8-10^12 axis this sits at ~79% of panel height, under a 10^-1-10^-5 (PFLOP) axis at ~98%; the rendered flat line sits at roughly 80% of panel height, which favours the raw-FLOP reading, but this is an estimate from a low-resolution render, not a measurement. NOT VERIFIED: I could not read the superscripts at print size and did not inspect the source file.
issue.acceptance_test: Inspect the source/vector PDF at 100% zoom and confirm the left panel's y-ticks read 10^14, 10^15, 10^16, 10^17 and the right panel's read 10^8, 10^9, 10^10, 10^11, 10^12 (raw FLOP). If they read 10^-1..10^2 and 10^-1..10^-5, the axis titles must be changed to PFLOP (or the data rescaled) - this would be a P0. Independently, increase the tick-label size so the exponents are readable at 100% print size (target >= 8 pt including the exponent), and add an explicit unit multiplier if any axis is not in base FLOP.

issue.figure: Figure 22.1, right panel (DECODE per token) legend
issue.issue: The right panel's legend carries two entries - 'decode 2*N (per token)' and 'PARAMETER term only' - but only one line is drawn. The two entries describe the same quantity, so the legend implies a second series that does not exist and invites the reader to hunt for it.
issue.evidence: Rendered right panel shows a single flat horizontal line. The caption confirms the intent: 'RIGHT = decode FLOPs/token (2N parameter term only, flat)'. The in-panel annotation '2*N only - full decode adds KV attention' already carries the 'parameter term only' qualifier, so the second legend entry is redundant with the annotation as well.
issue.acceptance_test: Reduce the right-panel legend to one entry ('decode 2*N per token (parameter term only)') or add the missing second series (the KV-attention term growing with context) so the legend matches the drawn content. A reader must not have to reconcile a legend entry with an absent line.

issue.issue: The right panel devotes roughly four decades of vertical axis to a single flat line, leaving most of the panel empty. The panel's job is to make one point - that the parameter term is independent of context length - and that point is made by the flatness, which is diluted by the empty space.
issue.evidence: Rendered right panel: one horizontal line in the upper portion, three-plus decades of unused grid below it. The left panel, which carries the actual crossover argument, is comparatively cramped.
issue.acceptance_test: Tighten the right panel's y-range to the band the flat line occupies (plus a small margin), or add the KV-attention term as a second curve so the panel carries information proportional to its area.

issue.figure: Figure 19.3 (State-management policy at four agent turns), dashed reference line
issue.issue: The dashed vertical line labelled 'single-shot reference 24.9 GB' appears to be drawn at roughly 20 GB on the axis, not at 24.9 GB. It sits visibly to the LEFT of the right edge of the Compaction bar, which is itself labelled '~24.9 GB'. A reference marker that does not land on the value it labels, and does not coincide with the bar it is supposed to coincide with, is a semantic error in the figure's central visual claim.
issue.evidence: Axis calibration from the rendered page: '0' at the left spine, '40' at the right spine, with 10-unit ticks between. The dashed line's x-position falls between the 20 and 30 ticks, near 20; the Compaction bar's right edge falls near 24-25. The figure's own arithmetic (printed below the axes) gives single-shot = I_0 + O_final = 9,200 + 300 = 9,500 tokens x 2.62 MB/token = 24.89 GB, and the compaction bar is labelled '~24.9 GB', so the two must coincide. NOT VERIFIED: I could not measure the pixel positions precisely at the rendered resolution; this needs confirmation against the vector source.
issue.acceptance_test: Measure the dashed line's x-coordinate against the axis scale in the source file: it must land at 24.9 GB, coincident with the right edge of the Compaction bar and at 73% of the Append-only bar's length (24.9/34.0). If it is at 20 GB, move it to 24.9 GB.

issue.issue: The label '34.0 GB unchanged' extends past the right end of the plotting area (the axis ends at 40 GB) and into the surrounding text block, whereas the other two value labels sit inside the axes. The overflow is small but it breaks the figure's right-hand alignment and makes the label look detached from its bar.
issue.evidence: Rendered page: the '34.0 GB unchanged' label begins at the bar end (~34 GB) and runs past the axis end at 40 GB; the '34.0 GB' and '~24.9 GB' labels are shorter and remain within the axes.
issue.acceptance_test: Either shorten the label to '34.0 GB' (the word 'unchanged' is already carried by the caption and the bar's hatch) or extend the x-axis to 45 GB so all three labels sit inside the axes.

issue.figure: Figure 20.1 (Fleet capacity vs host count), red annotation in the shaded region
issue.issue: The red annotation reads 'insufficient offered demand, 5 capped at 40 rps - not scheduling overhead'. The glyph before 'capped' renders as '5' but the quantity being capped is S (the actually-served demand), as defined in the legend ('actually-served demand S = min(40, C_eff)'). If the source really contains '5', this is a typo that names a non-existent quantity in the figure's key takeaway.
issue.evidence: Legend defines S = min(40, C_eff); the caption repeats 'actually-served demand S = min(40, C_eff)'. No quantity named '5' exists anywhere in the figure. At the rendered resolution 'S' and '5' are not reliably distinguishable, so this must be checked in the source. NOT VERIFIED against source.
issue.acceptance_test: Confirm the source glyph is 'S' (i.e. 'S capped at 40 rps'); if it is '5', correct it. The annotation must name a quantity defined in the same figure's legend.

issue.issue: The caption's parenthetical reads '(17/8.6 = 1.977 + 2.0 req/s/host x ~95% throughput-efficiency derate)'. The '+' between 1.977 and 2.0 is not a valid relation between two values of the same quantity; the intended operator is almost certainly '~' or '~=' (1.977 ~ 2.0 req/s/host). As printed it reads as an arithmetic sum, which is meaningless.
issue.evidence: 17/8.6 = 1.9767 req/s/host; the figure title states '(17 contexts / 8.6 s per host)'. The '+' is inconsistent with every other relation in the same sentence, which uses '=' and 'x'.
issue.acceptance_test: Replace '+' with '~' (or '~=') so the caption reads '17/8.6 = 1.977 ~ 2.0 req/s/host x ~95% throughput-efficiency derate'.

issue.figure: Figure 20.1, legend vs plotted line styles

issue.figure: Figure 21.1 (AI Factory promotion), FAIL band vs caption
issue.issue: The caption says 'each labelled FAIL branch restores last-known-good state and re-validates', but the figure draws a single continuous red FAIL band spanning all six gates with one label, not six labelled FAIL branches. The caption describes a per-gate structure the figure does not show, so a reader looking for the six branches finds one bar.
issue.evidence: Rendered page: one wide red rectangle labelled 'FAIL' with the sub-label 'rollback to last-known-good + re-validate' beneath it, spanning the full width under the six gate boxes. The figure's own text says 'Gates check data validity, training cost, eval quality, canary health, TTFT, and promotion cost; a breach rolls back' - singular 'a breach', consistent with the drawing but not with the caption's 'each labelled FAIL branch'.
issue.acceptance_test: Either draw six short FAIL stubs, one under each gate box, each labelled FAIL, or change the caption to 'a single FAIL band: any gate failure rolls back to last-known-good and re-validates'. Caption and drawing must agree on whether FAIL is per-gate or global.

issue.issue: The caption states 'Production feedback returns evidence to data/evaluation', but the figure's green feedback arrow terminates only at the Data box; there is no return path to Eval. The figure therefore under-draws a claim the caption makes, and the 'evaluation' half of the loop is invisible.
issue.evidence: Rendered page: the green line runs from beneath Serve leftward along the bottom and turns up into the Data box (arrowhead at Data). No green connector reaches the Eval box.

issue.figure: Figure 23.1 (From a vague ask to architectural bounds), box 4
issue.issue: Box 4 ('What are the constraints?') reads '8 x H100 host; ~14.6K/mo, no SLO headroom'. The monetary figure has no currency symbol, so '14.6K/mo' is uninterpretable on its face - it could be read as requests/month, tokens/month, or dollars/month. The figure's own box 5 uses '$/mo' as a quantity to quantify, and the caption refers to 'the cost ceiling in §23.3', so the intended reading is dollars per month. The missing '$' also hides an elegant internal consistency the figure should be making explicit: $14.6K/mo is exactly one 8 x H100 host at the canonical $20/hour on-demand rate for 730 hours/month ($20 x 730 = $14,600), which is precisely why the constraint box names a single host.
issue.evidence: Rendered page: box 4 shows '~14.6K/mo' with no '$' visible. Cross-checks: box 5 lists 'p95 TTFT, peak rps, hit rate, $/mo' (so '$/mo' is the book's notation for the cost quantity); the caption says 'the cost ceiling in §23.3 supplies the quality bar'; the canonical host cost on printed page 358 is '~$20/hour (cloud, $2.50/GPU-hr canonical)', and 8 GPUs x $2.50 = $20/hour, x 730 h = $14,600/month = $14.6K/month. NOT VERIFIED: whether the '$' is present in the source but illegible at the rendered resolution.
issue.acceptance_test: Confirm the source string is '~$14.6K/mo'; if the '$' is absent, add it. Additionally, make the one-host equivalence explicit in the box or the caption (e.g. '~$14.6K/mo = 1 host at $20/h x 730 h'), so the reader can see why a single 8 x H100 host is the binding constraint against the 40 rps peak in box 2.

issue.issue: The second line of the green box ('decisions enabled: KV FP16->FP8 + prefix cache + routing') appears to touch or overflow the box's left and right borders. Because the text is white on a dark green fill, any character that spills outside the box falls onto the white page and becomes invisible - a silent loss of content at the ends of the line, which is where 'KV FP16->FP8' and 'routing' sit.
issue.evidence: Rendered page: the green box spans a fixed width and the white text line appears to begin at or slightly left of the left border and end at or slightly right of the right border, with no visible padding. The five orange boxes above use visibly generous padding, so the green box is inconsistent with the figure's own spacing standard. NOT VERIFIED: exact overflow could not be measured at the rendered resolution; confirm in the vector source.
issue.acceptance_test: In the source, confirm the text line's rendered width is at least 4 mm narrower than the green box's inner width (or widen the box / shorten the text). A print proof at 100% must show the full string 'decisions enabled: KV FP16->FP8 + prefix cache + routing' with visible green padding on both sides and no white-on-white characters.

issue.figure: Figure 24.1 (Red Team / Green Team cycle), subtitle
issue.issue: The subtitle reads '(1->4 forward cycle; one red feedback loop back to step 1)'. The forward cycle in the figure is 1 -> 2 -> 3 -> 4 -> 5 -> 6 (Red Team -> Probes -> Exposure -> Guardrails -> Metrics -> Green Team), as the caption itself states. '1->4' misdescribes the cycle and excludes steps 5 and 6, which are drawn as part of the forward path. A reader who trusts the subtitle will read the figure as a four-step cycle with two trailing boxes.
issue.evidence: Rendered page: six numbered boxes with forward arrows 1->2->3->4->5->6; the caption enumerates all six ('red team -> probe -> exposure -> guardrails -> metrics -> green team'). The subtitle's '1->4' matches neither the drawing nor the caption.
issue.acceptance_test: Change the subtitle to '(1->6 forward cycle; one red feedback loop back to step 1)'. The step range in the subtitle must match the number of forward arrows drawn.
